definition_zh: 影响；感动；假装；患有（疾病）
definition_en: to produce a change in someone or something, to move the feelings, to pretend to feel something, or to be suffering from an illness
core_image: 一颗石子落进平静的水面，涟漪一圈圈推到岸边
scene: 坏消息传来时，会议室里没人说话。The news affected everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里的 affect 是「影响」（第 1 个义项：对人或事物产生作用）；句意是这条消息影响了屋里的每个人。

pos.zh: 动词：影响；感动；假装；患有

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「喜爱；感情」
过去分词转作形容词，义为「受到影响的；做作的」
现在分词转作形容词，义为「动人的；令人感伤的」
加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「不满的；不忠的」

senses.title: To produce a change in something
senses.definition: to cause a change in a person, thing, or situation, often without intending to
senses.definitionCN: 使人、事物或情形发生变化，常非有意为之
senses.example: The news affected everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息影响了屋里的每个人。
senses.why: Latin afficere meant to do something to a thing; the English verb keeps that outward push of one thing upon another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 afficere 意为「对某物施加作用」；英语动词保留了这种一物推向另一物的外力。

senses.title: To move the feelings
senses.definition: to touch someone emotionally, often strongly
senses.definitionCN: 在情感上打动某人，程度常较深
senses.example: The letters from the children affected him more than he expected.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们的信比他预想的更让他感动。
senses.why: The same push can land on the feelings rather than on circumstances; what is affected is then the heart.
senses.whyCN: 同一种推力可以落在情感上而不是境况上；这时被作用的是人心。

senses.title: To pretend to have a feeling
senses.definition: to behave as if you have a quality or feeling that you do not really have
senses.definitionCN: 表现得好像拥有某种其实并不具备的品质或感受
senses.example: He affected indifference whenever her name was mentioned.
senses.exampleCN: 每当有人提到她的名字，他就装作不在意。
senses.why: A person can also push a false appearance outward on purpose, and the verb then names that controlled display.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以故意向外推出一个虚假的外表，这时动词指的就是这种受控的展示。

senses.title: To be suffering from an illness
senses.definition: to be attacked or troubled by a disease or condition, used mostly in passive forms
senses.definitionCN: 受到疾病或病症侵袭，多用于被动形式
senses.example: The cattle were affected with a disease of the joints.
senses.exampleCN: 这些牛患上了关节疾病。
senses.why: In medicine the outward push becomes an affliction: the body is acted upon by the disease, so the passive form is usual.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，这种外力变成病痛：身体被疾病施加作用，因此常用被动形式。

intro.en: A Latin verb of doing something to something, narrowed in English to influence and feeling.
intro.cn: 一个表示「对某物施加作用」的拉丁动词，在英语里收窄为「影响」与「情感」。

items.en: facere meant to do or make, the base of fact, effect, factory and this verb.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，是 fact、effect、factory 与这个动词的底子。

items.en: ad 'to' plus facere 'do' formed afficere, to do something to a person or thing, to act upon it.
items.cn: ad（向）加 facere（做）构成 afficere，意为对某人某物施加作用。

items.en: The participle affectus meant 'acted upon' and also named a state of mind or feeling.
items.cn: 分词 affectus 意为「被作用的」，也用来指心境或情感状态。

items.en: Old French affecter meant to desire, seek, or pretend, and gave English the 'pretend' sense.
items.cn: 古法语 affecter 意为「欲求、追求、假装」，给英语留下了「假装」这一义项。

items.en: Modern English keeps affect for influence and feeling, while effect became the noun for a result.
items.cn: 现代英语用 affect 表示影响与感动，而 effect 则成为表示「结果」的名词。

note.en: The first group is the confusing -fect family; the second gathers verbs of influence, feeling, and pretence.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混淆的 -fect 词族；第二组收表示「影响、感动、假装」的动词。

entries.definition: a result; usually a noun, though it can be a verb meaning to bring about
entries.definitionCN: 结果；通常作名词，也可作动词表「实现」

entries.definition: a feeling of fondness
entries.definitionCN: 喜爱之情

entries.definition: influenced, or unnatural and pretended
entries.definitionCN: 受影响的；做作的

entries.definition: moving the feelings; touching
entries.definitionCN: 动人的；令人感伤的

entries.definition: to have an effect on how something develops
entries.definitionCN: 影响；对发展起作用

entries.definition: to cause strong feelings, especially sadness or sympathy
entries.definitionCN: 使感动；引起同情

entries.definition: to behave as if something is true when it is not
entries.definitionCN: 假装

entries.definition: to hit or to make a strong impression on someone
entries.definitionCN: 打击；给人强烈印象

normalIntro.en: The word is ad- plus facere, to do: to do something to someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 ad- 加 facere「做」：对某人做点什么。

normal.en: affect is a verb; effect is usually the noun for the result.
normal.cn: affect 是动词，effect 通常是表示结果的名词。

normal.en: ad- plus facere gives 'do to', which becomes influence.
normal.cn: ad- 加 facere 得出「对……做」，于是有了「影响」。

normal.en: The feelings sense survives in affection and affecting.
normal.cn: 情感义还活在 affection 与 affecting 里。

normal.en: To affect an accent is to put on a false one.
normal.cn: affect an accent 就是装出一种假口音。

normal.en: In medical writing the passive be affected with is common.
normal.cn: 医学文本里常用被动的 be affected with。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped in still water, rings reaching the bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落进静水，涟漪一路推到岸边。

abstract.en: See the same rings arriving not at sand but at a listener's face.
abstract.cn: 想象同样的涟漪不是拍到沙上，而是拍到一个听者的脸上。

abstract.cn: 想象一个人戴着平静的面具，面具下涟漪仍在动。

examples.en: Rising prices affect the poorest families most.
examples.cn: 物价上涨对最贫困的家庭影响最大。

examples.en: The story affected the whole audience.
examples.cn: 这个故事打动了全场观众。

examples.en: He affected a confidence he did not feel.
examples.cn: 他装出一副自己并不具备的自信。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of direction and the verb 'to do', with English endings building the family.
intro.cn: 一个方向前缀与表示「做」的拉丁动词，加上构成词族的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: facere, afficere and affectus are recorded Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: facere、afficere 与 affectus 都是有记录的拉丁形态。

definition_zh: 做作；矫饰；假装的姿态
definition_en: behaviour or speech that is not natural or sincere, adopted to impress other people
core_image: 戴上面具的脸：刻意摆出的姿态，与真实的自己隔了一层
scene: 聚会上，他忽然换了一口夸张的英式腔调。His British accent is just an affectation he picked up to impress his colleagues.
sceneCN: 这里 affectation 是「做作、矫饰」（第 2 个义项：为了给人留下印象而假装出的言行）；句意是说他那口英音不过是为了 impress 同事而刻意装出来的腔调。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「假装；影响」；affectation 由其名词化而来，语义偏移为「假作之态」
affect 加形容词后缀 -ed，义为「做作的；受影响的」
拼写相近的姊妹词，来自拉丁词根 afficere 的另一分支，义为「喜爱；感情」
affected 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「做作地；不自然地」

senses.title: An effort to appear to have a quality not really possessed
senses.definition: an attempt to seem to have a quality or feeling that one does not actually have
senses.definitionCN: 试图表现出某种自己并不真正具备的品质或感情
senses.example: Her modesty is an affectation; she loves being praised.
senses.exampleCN: 她的谦虚是装出来的；她其实很爱被夸奖。
senses.why: The Latin verb afficere came to mean to act upon or influence, so affectation is behaviour deliberately acted out rather than felt.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 afficere 有「施加作用」之意，affectation 由此长出「刻意演出来、并非真实感受」的核心义项。

senses.title: Artificial behaviour meant to impress others
senses.definition: unnatural or artificial manner or speech adopted to impress people
senses.definitionCN: 为了给人留下深刻印象而采取的不自然的言谈举止
senses.example: His British accent is just an affectation he picked up to impress his colleagues.
senses.exampleCN: 他那口英音不过是他在同事面前摆谱装出来的腔调。
senses.why: Once the acting-out sense settled, the word narrowed to the social fault of pretending refinement, hence artificiality aimed at impressing.
senses.whyCN: 「演出来」的含义固定后，词义收窄为社交上的毛病——假装高雅以讨好他人，即「做作、矫饰」。

senses.title: A particular habit or mannerism adopted for show
senses.definition: a specific habit, style, or mannerism that someone keeps up for effect
senses.definitionCN: 某人为了制造效果而长期保持的特定习惯、风格或小癖好
senses.example: Carrying an unopened umbrella everywhere is one of his affectations.
senses.exampleCN: 走到哪儿都带着一把从不打开的伞，是他的怪癖之一。
senses.why: A repeated pretence hardens into a fixed mannerism, so the countable sense of a single adopted habit grows from the same image.
senses.whyCN: 反复的假装会固化成一种固定的做派，于是从核心意象长出可数的「某一种刻意癖好」义项。

intro.en: From Latin afficere via the noun affectio; the meaning drifted from a state of mind to a pretended state of mind.
intro.cn: 源自拉丁语 afficere，经名词 affectio 传入英语；词义从「心境、状态」逐渐偏移为「假装出的心境」。

items.en: afficere meant to act upon, to influence; its noun affectio denoted a state or disposition of mind.
items.cn: 拉丁语 afficere 意为「作用于、影响」，其名词 affectio 表示心境或倾向的状态。

items.en: In later Latin, affectio also named an endeavour or striving toward something, preparing the pretending sense.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语中 affectio 又可指对某物的追求、意向，为「假装、佯作」一义埋下伏笔。

items.en: The word passed into Old French as affectacion, keeping the senses of striving and of an assumed state.
items.cn: 该词经古法语 affectacion 进入法语，保留「追求」与「假定的状态」两义。

items.en: Early English uses covered fondness and an endeavour to gain something, alongside the acting-out sense.
items.cn: 早期英语用法兼有「喜爱」「谋求某物」以及「假作」诸义。

items.en: The sense narrowed to artificial behaviour kept up to impress, the dominant modern meaning.
items.cn: 十七世纪起词义收窄为「为讨好他人而保持的做作言行」，成为现代主导义。

items.en: Today affectation almost always criticises insincerity; the fondness senses survive only in the separate word affection.
items.cn: 如今 affectation 几乎专用于批评不真诚；「喜爱」义只保留在另一个词 affection 里。

note.en: Affectation is easily confused with its sibling affection and with affected; only affectation means artificial pretence.
note.cn: affectation 极易与孪生词 affection 及 affected 混淆；只有 affectation 表示「做作、假态」。

entries.definition: the quality of being free from pretence or deceit

normalIntro.en: Build the word from affect plus the noun suffix -ation: something you act out.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 affect（假装）+ 名词后缀 -ation（行为），即「装出来的行为」。

normal.en: affect = to pretend; -ation makes it a noun, so affectation is an act of pretending
normal.cn: affect 意为「假装」，-ation 名词化，affectation 就是「假装的行为」

normal.en: affectation and affection differ by only one letter but one is fake and one is real love

normal.en: drop your affectations: take off the mask and behave naturally
normal.cn: drop your affectations 即「别装了」，摘下面具自然一点

normal.en: affected + -ion: an affected person shows an affectation
normal.cn: 做作的（affected）人表现出做作之态（affectation），词族互相印证

abstract.en: Picture a theatre mask clipped onto a real face: the show never stops
abstract.cn: 想象一张假面被夹在真脸上：戏一场接一场，从不下台

abstract.en: See someone speaking with a fake accent in a mirror, performing only for an audience that is not there
abstract.cn: 看见有人对着镜子用假腔调讲话，只为并不存在的观众表演

abstract.en: Imagine love (affection) wearing a costume; take the costume off and only affectation remains
abstract.cn: 想象爱（affection）穿上戏服；戏服一脱，剩下的只有做作

examples.en: She spoke with an air of affectation, dropping French phrases into every sentence.
examples.cn: 她说话做作得很，每句话都要夹一句法语。

examples.en: His rough manners are pure affectation; at home he is quite refined.
examples.cn: 他那副粗鲁做派纯属装出来的；在家时他相当斯文。

examples.en: The actress performed without affectation, and the audience felt her sincerity.
examples.cn: 这位女演员的表演毫不做作，观众感受到了她的真诚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆客淡定」——阿婆假斯文见客却装得淡定，其实浑身不自在，正是「做作」。谐音仅助记，并非词源。

definition_zh: 亲和力；亲近感；密切关系；相似性
definition_en: a natural liking for and understanding of someone or something; a close resemblance or relationship
core_image: 磁石相吸：两块石头隔着空气不由自主地靠近
scene: 她一走进那间老书店就感到说不出的自在。She has always felt a strong affinity for old bookshops and their dusty smell.
sceneCN: 这里 affinity 是「天然的亲近感」（第 1 个义项：自然而然的喜爱与投契）；句意是她对旧书店与那里的尘土气味一直怀有强烈的亲近感。

pos.zh: 亲近感；亲和力；密切关系

derivatives.zh: affinity 的形容词形态之一，义为「姻亲的」
同根动词 affilare 一支传入，义为「使隶属于；接纳为成员」
affiliate 加名词后缀 -ion，义为「附属关系；归属」
同根拉丁 filius（儿子）直接派生，义为「子女的；孝顺的」

senses.title: A natural liking and understanding of someone or something
senses.definition: a spontaneous feeling of sympathy and understanding between people, or a natural liking for something
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间自发的同情与默契，或对某事物的天然喜爱
senses.example: She has always felt a strong affinity for old bookshops and their dusty smell.
senses.exampleCN: 她对旧书店以及那里的尘土气味一直怀有强烈的亲近感。
senses.why: The Latin root finis means boundary; affinity originally meant being close by marriage, and closeness grew into the feeling of being naturally drawn together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 finis 意为「边界」；affinity 本指「因联姻而亲近」，由空间之近长出「天然相吸、一见投契」的情感义。

senses.title: A structural or qualitative resemblance between things
senses.definition: a close similarity between things, especially in structure or origin
senses.definitionCN: 事物之间在结构或来源上的高度相似
senses.example: Linguists noticed an affinity between the two ancient languages.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学家注意到这两种古代语言之间的相似性。
senses.why: Two things that seem bound together as if related share a kinship, so the relationship sense extends from people to objects and systems.
senses.whyCN: 两个仿佛有亲缘、被绑在一起的东西，就像有血缘一样；于是「关系」义从人扩展到物与体系，成为「相似性」。

senses.title: Relationship by marriage rather than by blood
senses.definition: kinship created by marriage, as opposed to consanguinity
senses.definitionCN: 因婚姻而产生的亲属关系，与血亲相对
senses.example: In law, affinity connects a husband to his wife's family.
senses.exampleCN: 在法律上，姻亲关系把丈夫与妻子的家族联系在一起。
senses.why: This is the historical core: marriage binds two families together, and the word kept the legal sense even after the figurative senses flourished.
senses.whyCN: 这是词义的历史内核：婚姻把两个家族绑在一起；即使比喻义蓬勃发展，法律上的「姻亲」义仍保留至今。

senses.title: The tendency of substances to combine chemically
senses.definition: the force by which atoms or molecules are attracted to and combine with others
senses.definitionCN: 原子或分子相互吸引并结合的力
senses.example: Oxygen shows a high affinity for iron in rusting.
senses.exampleCN: 生锈时，氧对铁表现出很强的亲和力。
senses.why: Science borrowed the image of natural attraction: substances drawn to each other behave like people with an affinity, hence chemical affinity.
senses.whyCN: 科学借用了「天然相吸」的意象：互相吸引的物质就像投契的人一样，于是有了「化学亲和力」。

intro.en: From Latin affinitas, built on finis (boundary), through Old French into English; the core idea is connection beyond a boundary.
intro.cn: 源自拉丁语 affinitas，建立在 finis（边界）之上，经古法语进入英语；核心观念是「跨越边界而联结」。

items.en: The reconstructed root *dhe- (to set, to fix) underlies Latin figere and the boundary word finis.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *dhe-（立、定）是拉丁语 figere 与边界词 finis 的远源。

items.en: affinis meant neighbouring, related by marriage (ad + finis, reaching the boundary of another family); affinitas named such kinship.
items.cn: 拉丁语 affinis 意为「毗邻的、因婚姻而结亲的」（ad + finis，触到别家的边界），affinitas 即这种姻亲关系。

items.en: afinite kept the kinship sense and began to suggest general closeness.
items.cn: 古法语 afinite 保留亲属关系义，并开始带出泛指的「亲近」。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word chiefly for relationship by marriage.
items.cn: 中古英语借入该词，主要用于「姻亲关系」。

items.en: The senses widened to natural liking and structural resemblance, then to chemical attraction.
items.cn: 十七至十九世纪词义扩展到「天然喜爱」「结构相似」，再到「化学亲和力」。

items.en: The emotional sense of natural rapport now dominates everyday use; the legal sense survives in technical contexts.
items.cn: 现代英语中「天然的投契感」主导日常用法；法律义只保留在专业语境。

note.en: Affinity overlaps with rapport and sympathy but adds the idea of a natural, almost magnetic pull.
note.cn: affinity 与 rapport、sympathy 意义交错，但多了一层天然的、近乎磁石般的相互吸引。

entries.definition: the state of having no end or limit
entries.definitionCN: 无穷；无限——同根 finis（边界），in- 加否定，边界消失即无限

entries.definition: the invasion of a body by disease-causing organisms
entries.definitionCN: 感染；传染——只是拼写相近，词源不同（拉丁 inficere）

entries.definition: the state of being formally attached to a group
entries.definitionCN: 附属；隶属关系——同族词，强调组织归属而非情感吸引

entries.definition: a statement asserting something strongly
entries.definitionCN: 断言；肯定——拼写相近但来自 firmus（坚固），词源不同

entries.definition: a close and harmonious relationship in which people understand each other
entries.definitionCN: 融洽；默契——强调互动顺畅，affinity 强调天生相吸

entries.definition: a feeling of pity or shared emotion
entries.definitionCN: 同情；同感——偏向怜悯与共情，affinity 偏向投契

entries.definition: blood relationship or a feeling of being related
entries.definitionCN: 亲属关系；亲近感——保留 affinity 的「亲缘」意象

entries.definition: a force drawing things or people together
entries.definitionCN: 吸引力——广义的吸引，含物理与情感

entries.definition: a strong feeling of dislike
entries.definitionCN: 厌恶；反感——affinity 的情感反义

normalIntro.en: Split the word as af- (toward) + fin (boundary) + -ity: reaching across a boundary to connect.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 af-（朝向）+ fin（边界）+ -ity（名词后缀）：越过边界去联结。

normal.en: af + fin + ity: toward the boundary of another family, i.e. marriage kinship
normal.cn: af+fin+ity：触到另一家的边界，即「姻亲」本义

normal.en: infinity shares the root fin: no boundary versus reaching a boundary
normal.cn: infinity 同根 fin：一个无边无界，一个跨过边界，对照记忆

normal.en: feel an affinity with someone: you click without trying
normal.cn: feel an affinity with someone 就是「一见如故」，不费力就合拍

normal.en: chemical affinity: atoms that 'like' each other combine
normal.cn: chemical affinity：互相「来电」的原子会结合，意象同情感义相通

normal.en: a natural affinity for music: born loving it
normal.cn: a natural affinity for music 即「天生爱音乐」，天性使然

abstract.en: Two magnets rolling toward each other across a table, unprompted
abstract.cn: 两块磁石隔着桌面不由自主地滚向彼此

abstract.en: A bridge spanning the boundary line between two estates, built by a wedding
abstract.cn: 一座跨越两家地界的桥，由一场婚礼建成

abstract.en: Two rivers of different colors merging smoothly into one stream
abstract.cn: 两条颜色不同的河顺畅地汇成一股水流

examples.en: He felt an immediate affinity with the young violinist, as if they had grown up together.
examples.cn: 他对那位年轻小提琴手一见如故，仿佛两人是一起长大的。

examples.en: Scientists studied the affinity of the virus for human cells.
examples.cn: 科学家研究了该病毒对人体细胞的亲和性。

examples.en: The report notes the close affinity between the two dialects.
examples.cn: 报告指出这两种方言之间的密切相似性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿凡提」——阿凡提骑毛驴走到哪都和百姓一见如故，亲和力十足。谐音仅助记，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ finis（边界、界限）构成 affinis「毗邻的、联姻的」，名词 affinitas 即「姻亲关系」；「跨越边界相联结」的核心意象引申出亲近感、相似性与亲和力诸义。

sensesIntro.en: From marriage kinship, the word stretches to natural rapport, structural resemblance, and chemical attraction.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「姻亲关系」出发，词义延伸到天然的投契、结构上的相似，再到化学上的亲和力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: magnets pulling across a boundary line
core.cn: 核心意象：隔着边界线相互吸引的磁石

branches.en: legal kinship by marriage
branches.cn: 法律上的姻亲关系，词义历史内核

branches.en: family ties that bind two houses
branches.cn: 把两家人绑在一起的亲属纽带

branches.en: spontaneous liking between people
branches.cn: 人与人之间不假思索的投契

branches.en: resemblance between languages, systems, or species
branches.cn: 语言、体系或物种之间的相似性

branches.en: attraction that combines things, chemical or emotional
branches.cn: 使事物结合的吸引力，化学与情感同象

intro.cn: 该词建立在拉丁词根 finis（边界、终点）之上，前缀 ad- 表朝向，后缀 -ity 名词化。

latinIntro.en: Other English words from the same root finis form a compact family.
latinIntro.cn: 英语中来自词根 finis 的同族词不多但很常用。

items.exampleCN: affinity（亲近）、infinity（无限）皆以 -ity 结尾
卧床不起（被限制在床上）

items.meaning: to set the limits of, to state precisely

由 ad（朝向）+ finis（边界）构成

latinEntries.example: passed into Old French as afinite
latinEntries.exampleCN: 经古法语 afinite 传入英语

使隶属；使加入（同族词）

definition_zh: （名词）词缀；附加物；（动词）附上；粘贴；盖（印）
definition_en: a letter or letters added to a word to form a new word; to attach or fasten something to a surface
core_image: 一枚被贴上去的小标签：附在词根或物体上
scene: 旧书摊的桌上放着一叠信封，摊主正把一枚邮票按在右上角。He affixed a stamp to the corner of the envelope.
sceneCN: 这里 affixed 是「贴上、粘上」（第 3 个义项：把某物固定到另一物表面）；句意为他把一枚邮票贴在信封的角上。画面中可辨识：旧书摊、信封、邮票。

derivatives.zh: 由 affix 加 -ation 构成，义为「词缀法；附加过程」
由 affix 加 -al 构成，义为「词缀的；与词缀有关的」

senses.title: A word element added to a root
senses.definition: a letter or group of letters added to the beginning or end of a word to change its meaning or form
senses.definitionCN: 加在词首或词尾、用以改变词义或词形的字母或字母组合
senses.example: The prefix un- is a common affix in English.
senses.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 是英语中常见的词缀。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the physical verb: a prefix or suffix is fastened onto a root just as a label is fastened onto a box.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了这个物理动词：前缀或后缀就像标签贴到盒子上一样，被固定在词根上。

senses.title: Something attached as an addition
senses.definition: a thing attached or added to something else, often as a minor addition
senses.definitionCN: 附加或添加到另一物上的东西，常指次要的添加物
senses.example: The contract had a short affix listing two extra duties.
senses.exampleCN: 合同后面附了一份简短的附加条款，列出两项额外义务。
senses.why: The noun keeps the literal sense: whatever has been fastened on becomes an affix.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了字面义：凡是被固定上去的东西，就成为一个 affix。

senses.title: To attach or fasten to a surface
senses.definition: to attach, fasten, or stick something onto a surface or object
senses.definitionCN: 把某物附着、固定或粘贴到某个表面或物体上
senses.example: He affixed a stamp to the corner of the envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一枚邮票贴在信封的角上。
senses.why: The Latin past participle meant fastened to, and the verb still means exactly that, with no metaphor needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语过去分词意为「固定于」，这个动词至今仍是这个意思，完全不需要比喻。

senses.title: To add a signature or seal
senses.definition: to add a signature, seal, or mark to a document in a formal way
senses.definitionCN: 在文件上正式加上签名、印章或标记
senses.example: Both parties affixed their seals to the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 双方都在协议上盖了章。
senses.why: A seal is literally pressed onto paper, so this official sense is only the physical act made legal.
senses.whyCN: 印章确实是压在纸上的，所以这个正式义只是把物理动作放进了法律程序。

intro.en: Affix comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to fasten to', and its grammatical sense is a later borrowing of that physical image.
intro.cn: affix 来自拉丁语动词「固定到」，其语法义是后来从这个物理意象借来的。

items.en: Figere meant 'to fasten, fix, drive in', and it also gave English fix.
items.cn: figere 意为「固定、钉入」，它也给了英语 fix 这个词。

items.en: Affigere meant 'to fasten to, attach', built from ad- and figere.
items.cn: affigere 意为「固定到、附上」，由 ad- 与 figere 构成。

items.en: The past participle affixus meant 'fastened to' and became the English noun and adjective stem.
items.cn: 过去分词 affixus 意为「固定于」，成为英语名词与形容词的词干。

items.en: English used affix first for a thing fastened on, then adopted it for word elements in grammar.
items.cn: 英语先用 affix 指被固定上去的东西，后来在语法中用它指词缀。

items.en: Affixation became the standard term for the process of adding prefixes and suffixes.
items.cn: affixation 成为表示添加前缀与后缀这一过程的标准术语。

note.en: The first group gathers words from the same 'fasten' root; the second gathers word-formation and attachment terms.
note.cn: 第一组收同一「固定」词根的一族词；第二组收构词与附着类术语。

entries.definition: The process of adding an affix to a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「词缀法；附加过程」，由 affix 加 -ation 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to an affix or to affixes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「词缀的」，由 affix 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: To repair something or fasten it in place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修理；固定」，与 affix 同出拉丁语 figere「固定」。

entries.definition: An affix added to the beginning of a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「前缀」，是 affix 的一种，位于词首。

entries.definition: An affix added to the end of a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后缀」，是 affix 的一种，位于词尾。

entries.definition: Something fastened or joined to another thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附件；附着物」，与义项二相近，但更强调连接关系。

normalIntro.en: Affix is best held by the word fix: an affix is something fixed onto something else.
normalIntro.cn: affix 可以靠 fix 这个词来记：affix 就是被固定到别处的东西。

normal.en: Fix means fasten, and af- is the assimilated form of ad-, so affix is to fasten to.
normal.cn: fix 意为「固定」，af- 是 ad- 的同化形式，所以 affix 就是「固定到」。

normal.en: A prefix is an affix at the front and a suffix is an affix at the end.
normal.cn: prefix 是位于词首的 affix，suffix 是位于词尾的 affix。

normal.en: To affix a stamp is the everyday physical use that keeps the original image alive.
normal.cn: affix a stamp「贴邮票」是让原始意象保持鲜活的日常用法。

normal.en: Affixation names the process, and affixal describes anything about affixes.
normal.cn: affixation 指这个过程，affixal 描述与词缀有关的事物。

normal.en: The noun stress falls on the first syllable, while the verb is often unstressed differently.
normal.cn: 名词重音落在第一个音节，动词的读法常常不同。

abstract.en: Picture a small sticker pressed onto the corner of a page, easy to miss but impossible to remove without a mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小贴纸压在书页角上，容易忽略，却一撕就会留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Think of a word as a body and an affix as a piece of clothing put on at the edge.
abstract.cn: 把一个词想成身体，把词缀想成穿在边缘的一件衣服。

abstract.en: See the same hand that fixes a stamp also fixing meaning onto a root.
abstract.cn: 想象贴邮票的那只手，也在把意义固定到词根上。

examples.en: The affix -ness turns adjectives into nouns.
examples.cn: 词缀 -ness 把形容词变成名词。

examples.en: Please affix your signature to the bottom of the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格底部签上你的名字。

examples.en: The parcel had no return address on it.
examples.cn: 包裹上没有寄件人的地址。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿菲克斯」——阿（a）菲（fei）克（ke）斯（si），把东西固定上去，就像词缀贴在词根上。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 figere「固定」构成 affigere「固定到」，过去分词 affixus 成为英语的 affix；作动词时读「/əˈfɪks/」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a physical act of fastening, then splits into the thing fastened on and the grammar term for letters fastened to a root.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初是物理上的「固定」动作，随后分成两条线：被固定上去的东西，以及语法中固定在词根上的字母。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small label pressed onto a surface
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚压在某物表面的小标签

branches.en: Letters fastened to a root to make a new word.
branches.cn: 固定在词根上以构成新词的字母。

branches.en: Any object fastened on as an addition.
branches.cn: 作为附加物固定上去的任何物件。

branches.en: The physical act of sticking something on.
branches.cn: 把某物贴上去的物理动作。

branches.en: A seal or signature pressed onto a document.
branches.cn: 压在文件上的印章或签名。

branches.en: Everyday sticking and formal sealing as one action.
branches.cn: 日常粘贴与正式盖章是同一个动作。

intro.en: Affix is a Latin verb form that became both a noun and a verb in English, with a small but clear family.
intro.cn: affix 是拉丁语动词形式，在英语中同时成为名词与动词，词族不大却清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus figere produced affigere, whose participle affixus English borrowed directly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 figere 构成 affigere，英语直接借用了它的分词形式 affixus。

definition_zh: 富裕的；富足的；（地区）高档的；丰富的
definition_en: having a lot of money and a high standard of living; plentiful or abundant
core_image: 水源源不断流进来的样子：钱与资源充盈
scene: 河岸边的山坡上，新盖的房子一栋接一栋，花园里种着整齐的树。The affluent suburb has large houses, private schools, and quiet streets.
sceneCN: 这里 affluent 是「富裕的」（第 1 个义项：拥有大量钱财、生活水准高）；句意为这个富裕的郊区有大房子、私立学校和安静的街道。画面中可辨识：山坡住宅、花园、安静的街道。

derivatives.zh: 由 affluent 去掉词尾加 -ence 构成，义为「富裕；丰裕」
由 affluent 加 -ly 构成，义为「富裕地；丰足地」
由 affluent 与 influenza 缩合而成，指过度追求物质带来的「富裕病」，属非正式用词

senses.title: Having plenty of money
senses.definition: having a great deal of money and a high standard of living
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量钱财、生活水准很高
senses.example: The affluent couple donated a large sum to the library.
senses.exampleCN: 这对富裕的夫妇向图书馆捐了一大笔钱。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to flow toward, and the image is resources flowing in without stopping.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「流向」，意象是资源不停地流进来。

senses.title: Of a place: wealthy and comfortable
senses.definition: of an area or neighbourhood, inhabited by wealthy people and offering expensive services
senses.definitionCN: 指地区或街区住着富裕人群、提供昂贵服务
senses.example: They moved to an affluent suburb with a private school nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬到了一个附近有私立学校的富裕郊区。
senses.why: Wealth spreads across a map: when many rich households cluster, the place itself is called affluent.
senses.whyCN: 财富会铺到地图上：当许多富裕家庭聚集，这个地方本身就被称为 affluent。

senses.title: Existing in abundance
senses.definition: present in large quantities; plentiful, used especially in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 大量存在的、充裕的，尤用于正式书面语
senses.example: The valley had affluent supplies of water and timber.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷拥有充裕的水源和木材。
senses.why: The original sense was simply flowing plentifully, before money narrowed the word in everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 最初的意思只是「大量流动」，在日常生活里才被钱的意义收窄。

senses.title: Flowing freely, in older use
senses.definition: flowing freely or in abundance, an older and now rare sense
senses.definitionCN: 自由地或大量地流动，这一义项较古老，现今罕用
senses.example: The old poem describes an affluent stream that never dries.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古老的诗描写一条永不干涸的丰沛溪流。
senses.why: Before it named money, the word described water moving in quantity; that literal sense survives mainly in old texts.
senses.whyCN: 在指钱之前，这个词描述的是大量流动的水；这一字面义主要残留在旧文本里。

intro.en: Affluent is built on a Latin verb for flowing, and wealth was originally pictured as a flow of resources.
intro.cn: affluent 建立在拉丁语表示「流动」的动词上，财富最初被想象成资源的流动。

items.en: Fluere meant 'to flow', and it also gave English fluent and fluid.
items.cn: fluere 意为「流动」，它也给了英语 fluent 与 fluid。

items.en: Affluere meant 'to flow to, to flow in abundance', built with ad- and fluere.
items.cn: affluere 意为「流向、大量涌入」，由 ad- 与 fluere 构成。

items.en: Affluentia named abundance and the flow of wealth or supplies.
items.cn: affluentia 指丰裕，以及财富或物资的流入。

items.en: English first used affluent for flowing abundantly, then for people with abundant means.
items.cn: 英语最初用 affluent 表示「大量流动」，后来才指拥有丰裕资财的人。

items.en: The wealth sense became dominant, while the literal water sense retreated to older texts.
items.cn: 财富义成为主流，字面的水流义退回到旧文本中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same 'flow' root; the near-meaning group gathers words for wealth and comfort.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「流动」词根的一族词；近义组收表示财富与富足生活的词。

entries.definition: A state of having a lot of money and material goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「富裕；丰裕」，是 affluent 的名词形式。

entries.definition: Able to speak or write a language easily and smoothly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「流利的」，与 affluent 同出拉丁语 fluere「流动」，但前缀不同。

entries.definition: The place where two rivers flow together, or a coming together of things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「汇流处；汇集」，同样来自 fluere「流动」。

entries.definition: Having a large amount of money, property, or valuable things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富有的」，与 affluent 义项一几乎同义，更直白。

entries.definition: Successful and financially strong, especially of a person or region.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「繁荣的；兴旺的」，侧重发展与成功，而非单纯拥有钱财。

entries.definition: Having enough money to live comfortably.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽裕的；日子好过的」，程度比 affluent 温和。

entries.definition: Existing in large amounts, more than enough.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充足的；大量的」，对应义项三，但不含财富义。

normalIntro.en: Affluent is anchored by the root flu, which means flow, and by the picture of money flowing in.
normalIntro.cn: affluent 可以靠表示「流动」的词根 flu，以及钱不断流入的画面来记。

normal.en: Flu means flow, and affluere means to flow toward, so affluent is 'flowing in with resources'.
normal.cn: flu 意为「流动」，affluere 意为「流向」，所以 affluent 就是「资源源源流入」。

normal.en: Affluence is the noun for the state, and affluently is the adverb.
normal.cn: affluence 是表示状态的名词，affluently 是副词。

normal.en: An affluent suburb is a place where wealthy households cluster.
normal.cn: affluent suburb 是富裕家庭聚集的地方。

normal.en: Fluent and fluid share the same root, which keeps the flow image in view.
normal.cn: fluent 与 fluid 共享同一词根，让「流动」的意象始终可见。

normal.en: The phrase the affluent treats the adjective as a collective noun.
normal.cn: 「the affluent」这个说法把形容词当作集合名词使用。

abstract.en: Picture a river of coins running past a house and never running dry.
abstract.cn: 想象一条硬币组成的河从房前流过，永不干涸。

abstract.en: Think of a garden where the sprinkler is always on and the soil is always dark with water.
abstract.cn: 想象一座花园，喷头一直开着，土壤总是被水浸得发黑。

abstract.en: See wealth as a current rather than a pile: what matters is how much keeps arriving.
abstract.cn: 把财富看成水流而不是堆叠：重要的是有多少在不断到来。

examples.en: The affluent neighbourhood has its own marina and tennis club.
examples.cn: 这个富裕的街区有自己的游艇码头和网球俱乐部。

examples.en: Affluent families often spend more on tutoring than on holidays.
examples.cn: 富裕家庭花在辅导上的钱常常比花在度假上的更多。

examples.en: The river ran clear after the spring rains.
examples.cn: 春雨过后，河水清澈地流着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿弗伦特」——阿（a）弗（fu）伦（lun）特（te），钱像水一样不断流进来，日子就富裕了。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 fluere「流动」构成 affluere「流入、丰沛」，其名词 affluentia 指丰裕；英语先指「大量流动」，后专指富裕。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as water flowing in abundance, then narrows to money, then widens again to rich places and plentiful supplies.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初指水大量流动，后收窄为钱财，再扩展为富裕地区与充裕物资。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: resources flowing in like a stream
core.cn: 核心意象：资源像溪流一样不断流入

branches.en: Money flowing into a household.
branches.cn: 钱财流入家庭。

branches.en: Wealth written across a whole district.
branches.cn: 财富铺展在整个街区。

branches.en: Supplies present in large quantity.
branches.cn: 大量存在的物资。

branches.en: The old literal sense of water flowing freely.
branches.cn: 水流自由流动的古老字面义。

branches.en: Abundance in money and abundance in goods.
branches.cn: 钱财的丰裕与物资的丰裕。

intro.en: Affluent is a prefix plus the Latin root for flow, with a family that spreads across several everyday words.
intro.cn: affluent 是前缀加拉丁语「流动」词根，其词族分布在好几个日常词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus fluere made affluere, and fluentia supplied the noun affluence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 fluere 构成 affluere，fluentia 则提供了名词 affluence。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

latinEntries.example: Fluere is the root of affluent and fluent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fluere 是 affluent 与 fluent 的词根。
affluentia 给了英语 affluence。

definition_zh: 闹事；斗殴；当众骚乱
definition_en: a noisy public fight or disturbance, especially one that breaks the peace in public
core_image: 街角骤起的群架：叫喊声炸开，行人四散
scene: 深夜的地铁站台忽然乱作一团。Two men were charged with affray after a brawl broke out on the platform.
sceneCN: 这里 affray 是「当众斗殴、扰乱治安」（第 2 个义项：公共场合破坏安宁的打斗）；句意是两名男子因在站台斗殴而被控闹事罪。

derivatives.zh: affray 加表人后缀 -er，义为「挑起斗殴者；闹事者」（罕用）
同根古法语 effrei 的英语姊妹词，义为「惊吓」
fright 加动词后缀 -en，义为「使惊恐」
fright 加形容词后缀 -ful，义为「可怕的；糟糕的」

senses.title: An act of frightening or disturbing the peace
senses.definition: an action that frightens peaceful people and breaches public order
senses.definitionCN: 惊吓平静的民众、破坏公共秩序的行为
senses.example: The shouting alone constituted an affray under the old law.
senses.exampleCN: 按旧时法律，单是这阵叫喊就已构成惊扰治安罪。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning to frighten away, so its oldest sense is the disturbance itself rather than the fight.
senses.whyCN: 该词源自「吓走」的动词，因此最古老的义项是「惊扰」本身，而非打斗。

senses.title: A noisy public fight involving several people
senses.definition: a fight in a public place, typically involving three or more people, that terrifies bystanders
senses.definitionCN: 公共场合的打斗，通常三人或以上参与，令旁观者惊恐
senses.example: Two men were charged with affray after a brawl broke out on the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 两名男子因在站台斗殴而被控闹事罪。
senses.why: Because frightening the public is the legal core, any violent group brawl in public naturally falls under this sense.
senses.whyCN: 由于「惊吓公众」是法律核心，公共场合的群体斗殴自然归入此义项，成为现代主导用法。

senses.title: A noisy quarrel or commotion generally
senses.definition: any noisy disturbance or heated quarrel, without strict legal meaning
senses.definitionCN: 泛指嘈杂的骚动或激烈的争吵，不带严格法律含义
senses.example: The cabinet meeting ended in an undignified affray over the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 内阁会议最终因预算问题闹得不欢而散、一片喧哗。
senses.why: Once the legal sense was established, everyday speech stretched the image of public uproar to any messy quarrel.
senses.whyCN: 法律义确立后，日常语言把「当众喧闹」的意象放宽，用来戏称任何混乱的争吵。

intro.en: From Old French effrei / esfreer (to frighten away), of Frankish origin; the core idea is frightening the public.
intro.cn: 源自古法语 effrei / esfreer（吓走），一般认为出自法兰克语；核心观念是「惊吓公众」。

items.en: A reconstructed Frankish verb (cf. German befremden, to unsettle) is generally taken as the ultimate source.
items.cn: 一般认为重构的法兰克语动词（与德语 befremden「使不安」同族）是最终来源。

items.en: effrei meant fear or terror; the verb esfreer meant to frighten away, especially of driving off intruders.
items.cn: 古法语 effrei 意为「恐惧」，动词 esfreer 意为「吓走」，尤指赶走入侵者。

items.en: afray entered English legal language with the sense of disturbing the peace.
items.cn: 经由盎格鲁-诺曼语 afray 进入英语法律用语，意为「扰乱治安」。

items.en: Middle English used both the verb (to frighten) and the noun (terror, then a breach of peace).
items.cn: 中古英语中动词义「使惊吓」与名词义「恐惧」并存，后者渐转指「破坏安宁」。

items.en: The verb sense died out; the noun settled on public fighting as its legal meaning.
items.cn: 十六世纪起动词义消亡，名词义固定为「当众斗殴」这一法律含义。

items.en: Affray is now chiefly a legal term in Britain, with a looser figurative use for any uproar.
items.cn: 如今 affray 在英国主要是法律术语，另有一条宽泛的比喻用法指「喧闹、乱作一团」。

note.en: Affray is more formal and legal than brawl, and narrower than riot; its cousins fright and frighten share the frightening root.
note.cn: affray 比 brawl 更正式、更具法律色彩，又比 riot 范围窄；fright 与 frighten 是同根的「惊吓」词族。

entries.definition: a sudden intense fear
entries.definitionCN: 惊吓；惊恐——同根词，保留了词源里「惊吓」的核心

entries.definition: to make someone afraid
entries.definitionCN: 使惊恐——affray 词源动词的英语同族

entries.definition: an ordered arrangement, especially of troops
entries.definitionCN: 排列；阵列——拼写相近但词源不同（古法语 arayer，排列）

entries.definition: a brawl or battle
entries.definitionCN: 打斗；冲突——affray 的直接简短同源词

entries.definition: a rough noisy fight, usually in a public place
entries.definitionCN: 斗殴；喧闹的打斗——口语化，不带精确法律定义

entries.definition: a violent public disorder involving a crowd
entries.definitionCN: 暴乱；骚乱——规模更大、更严重的群体暴力

entries.definition: a confused struggle involving many people
entries.definitionCN: 混战；乱斗——强调混乱无序

entries.definition: an interruption of peaceful state or order
entries.definitionCN: 骚乱；干扰——泛指打破安宁的行为，未必有肢体冲突

entries.definition: a calm and orderly state
entries.definitionCN: 安宁；和平——affray 所破坏的状态

normalIntro.en: Split the word as af- + fray: a fray is already a fight, and affray lifts it into public and legal territory.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 af- + fray：fray 本身就是打斗，affray 则把它升级为公共与法律层面的闹事。

normal.en: fray = a fight; affray = a fight that frightens the public
normal.cn: fray 是打斗；affray 是吓到公众的打斗，即「闹事」

normal.en: be charged with affray: the phrase you will meet in British news
normal.cn: be charged with affray 是英国新闻里的常见说法：被控闹事罪

normal.en: fright and affray share one root: frighten first, fight second
normal.cn: fright 与 affray 同根：先「吓」，后「打」

normal.en: a street affray broke out: the usual collocation for sudden group brawls
normal.cn: a street affray broke out 是突发街头群架的惯用搭配

normal.en: riot > affray > brawl: from crowd violence down to a mere scuffle
normal.cn: riot（暴乱）＞ affray（闹事）＞ brawl（斗殴），严重程度递减

abstract.en: Bottles shattering on a pub floor while bystanders scatter
abstract.cn: 酒瓶在小酒馆地板上炸裂，行人四散奔逃

abstract.en: A gavel coming down hard while shouts erupt in a courtroom
abstract.cn: 法庭上一片喊声骤起，法槌重重落下

abstract.en: A fire alarm pulled as a prank: noise and panic without a real fire
abstract.cn: 恶作剧般拉响火警：没有真火，只有噪音与恐慌

examples.en: The football fans were arrested for affray outside the stadium.
examples.cn: 这些球迷因在体育场外闹事斗殴而被捕。

examples.en: What began as an argument ended in an affray that left two people injured.
examples.cn: 起初只是一场口角，最后演变成致两人受伤的斗殴。

examples.en: The debate descended into an affray of shouted slogans.
examples.cn: 辩论最后沦为一片口号声中的大乱斗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆怒易」——阿婆一看有人当街斗殴，怒气易起，喝止闹事。谐音仅助记，并非词源。

root: 一般认为源自法兰克语系动词（与德语 befremden「使不安」同族），经古法语 esfreer「吓走」、名词 effrei「恐惧」传入英语；核心意象是「惊吓公众」，法律上引申为「当众斗殴、扰乱治安」。

sensesIntro.en: From frightening the public, the word narrowed to public brawling in law, and widened again to any uproar in speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「惊扰公众」收窄为法律上的「当众斗殴」，又在日常语言中放宽为泛指的「喧闹骚动」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brawl that terrifies bystanders
core.cn: 核心意象：吓得旁观者四散的当众斗殴

branches.en: the alarm itself as an offence
branches.cn: 惊吓本身即构成违法行为

branches.en: violence that disturbs public order
branches.cn: 扰乱公共秩序的暴力行为

branches.en: several people fighting where others can see
branches.cn: 众目睽睽之下的群体斗殴

branches.en: from courtroom term to everyday quarrel
branches.cn: 从法庭术语放宽为日常争吵

branches.en: any scene of noisy disorder
branches.cn: 任何一片嘈杂混乱的场面

intro.en: The word preserves the prefix af- (ad-, toward) before a stem of Frankish origin; its closest English kin are fright and fray.
intro.cn: 该词保留前缀 af-（即 ad-，朝向），词干一般认为出自法兰克语；英语中最亲近的同族词是 fright 与 fray。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin ancestry, so there are no Latin cognates to list.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁语来源，因此没有可列的拉丁同族词。

items.exampleCN: affray、affix 等词中 f 前的 ad- 均写作 af-
enter the fray：投入战斗（常比喻参战争论）
把某人吓跑（正是词源本义）

items.meaning: to unsettle, to seem strange to
items.meaningCN: 使不安；使觉得怪异——一般认为与 affray 远同源
闹事者；挑起斗殴者（罕用）
排列；阵列——只是拼写相近，词源无关
背叛——拼写韵脚相近但词源无关

derivatives.zh: 打斗；冲突（同源简短形式）
惊吓（同根名词）
使惊恐（同根动词）
可怕的（fright 加 -ful）

definition_zh: 在进行中；酝酿中；徒步的
definition_en: in progress or being planned; on foot, walking
core_image: 脚步已迈出：事情正在路上，肉眼可见地展开
scene: 办公室里流言四起，人人神色紧张。Rumours of a merger were afoot long before the official announcement.
sceneCN: 这里 afoot 是「正在酝酿、进行中」（第 1 个义项：计划或活动已经在展开）；句意是合并的传言早在官方宣布之前就已四处流传。

pos.zh: 进行中的；酝酿中的（表语用法为主）

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「脚；英尺」；afoot 即 foot 的介词化组合
foot 复合名词，义为「小径；人行道」
foot 复合名词，义为「脚步声；客流」
同构词式 a- + fire，义为「燃烧着；激动不已」

senses.title: In progress or being planned
senses.definition: currently happening or being prepared, often secretly or without public confirmation
senses.definitionCN: 正在发生或正在筹划，常带有秘密进行、尚未公开的色彩
senses.example: Rumours of a merger were afoot long before the official announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 合并的传言早在官方宣布之前就已四处流传。
senses.why: The image is of feet already in motion: an undertaking has set out and cannot be seen fully yet, hence plans under way.
senses.whyCN: 意象是「脚步已经迈开」：一项行动已经上路、但全貌尚未可见，于是引申为「计划在酝酿推进中」。

senses.title: On foot; walking
senses.definition: travelling or moving on foot rather than by vehicle or horse
senses.definitionCN: 不乘车马、以双脚行进
senses.example: The pilgrims completed the last stage of their journey afoot.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者们徒步完成了旅程的最后一段。
senses.why: This is the literal layer: a- plus foot simply describes someone standing or moving on their feet.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面层：a-（处于状态）+ foot（脚），直接描写「双脚着地、以脚行进」的原始画面。

senses.title: In active circulation or existence
senses.definition: present and circulating among people, as rumours, diseases, or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 指流言、疾病、观念等正在人群中流传、存在
senses.example: Several strains of flu were afoot that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天有好几种流感病毒在流行。
senses.why: What is under way is also out and about among people, so the sense extends from plans to anything circulating actively.
senses.whyCN: 「在推进」的东西同时也在人群间流转，于是词义从「计划」扩展到一切正在活跃流传的事物。

intro.en: A native English formation: the prefix a- (on, in) plus foot, first literal, then figurative.
intro.cn: 英语本土构词：前缀 a-（处于……状态）+ foot（脚），先有字面义，后生比喻义。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ped- (foot) underlies foot and its Germanic cousins.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ped-（脚）是 foot 及其日耳曼同族词的远源。

items.en: on fote meant on foot; the phrase lived as two words.
items.cn: 古英语作 on fote，意为「以脚行进」，当时仍是短语形式。

items.en: The phrase fused into afoot, keeping the walking sense and adding the sense of in progress.
items.cn: 中古英语中短语融合为 afoot，保留「徒步」义，并新增「进行中」一义。

items.en: Shakespeare uses something is afoot in the figurative sense of stirrings under way.
items.cn: 莎士比亚笔下已用 something is afoot 表示「有动静、有事酝酿」。

items.en: The figurative sense now dominates; the walking sense survives mostly in literary or set phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语中比喻义占主导；「徒步」义主要残存于书面语和固定搭配。

note.en: Afoot signals ongoing movement, often with a hint of secrecy; underway and in motion are its plain neighbours.
note.cn: afoot 强调正在推进，常带一丝隐秘色彩；underway 与 in motion 是它的平义近邻。

entries.definition: burning; filled with excitement
entries.definitionCN: 燃烧着的；激动的——同款 a- 前缀构词，意象平行

entries.definition: on or into a ship, aircraft, or train
entries.definitionCN: 在船（车、机）上——同为 a- + 名词的组合

entries.definition: free to go or travel anywhere
entries.definitionCN: 自由自在、无牵挂的——同根 foot

entries.definition: coldly distant in manner
entries.definitionCN: 冷漠疏远的——拼写与 afoot 相似，词源不同（航海词 luff）

entries.definition: having started and in progress
entries.definitionCN: 进行中——平义近邻，无隐秘色彩

entries.definition: developing, especially trouble about to happen
entries.definitionCN: 酝酿中的（多指麻烦）——与 afoot 的隐秘义相合

entries.definition: awaiting decision or settlement
entries.definitionCN: 待决的；悬而未决的——强调等待而非推进

entries.definition: in movement; out of bed and active
entries.definitionCN: 活动起来的；骚动的——同为 a- 系状态词

entries.definition: temporarily inactive
entries.definitionCN: 休眠的；中止的——afoot 的反义状态

normalIntro.en: Read the word literally as a + foot: feet already moving, so the matter is under way.
normalIntro.cn: 把词读作 a + foot：脚已在动，事情自然「在路上」。

normal.en: something is afoot: the classic phrase for secret goings-on
normal.cn: something is afoot 是「有情况、有猫腻」的经典说法

normal.en: plans are afoot: they have set out but are not announced
normal.cn: plans are afoot：计划已启动但尚未公开

normal.en: afoot versus aloof: feet moving versus standing apart
normal.cn: afoot（脚步在动）对照 aloof（冷眼旁观），拼写一步之差

normal.en: afire, aboard, afoot: the a- family marks an active state
normal.cn: afire、aboard、afoot 同属 a- 家族，都表示「处于某状态」

normal.en: walk afoot: the old literal sense of travelling on foot
normal.cn: walk afoot 保留「徒步」的古义，帮助锚定词形

abstract.en: Boots stepping out of frame while only shadows show what is coming
abstract.cn: 一双靴子正迈出画面，只见影子不知来者

abstract.en: A pot lid rattling softly before the soup boils over
abstract.cn: 锅盖在汤滚溢之前轻轻地颤动作响

abstract.en: A train already moving as its destination sign flickers on

definition_zh: 重新；从头再来
definition_en: again, especially in a new or different way; starting from the beginning
core_image: 清零的画布：旧的一页翻过，重新落笔
scene: 项目失败后，团队没有抱怨，而是重整旗鼓。After the project failed, the team decided to start afresh with a smaller plan.
sceneCN: 这里 afresh 是「重新开始」（第 1 个义项：从零起步、以新的方式再做）；句意是项目失败后团队决定换个更小的方案从头再来。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「新鲜的；清新的」；afresh 即 fresh 的副词化
fresh 加动词后缀 -en，义为「使新鲜；使清爽」
re- + fresh，义为「使恢复精力；刷新」
refresh 加形容词后缀 -ing，义为「令人耳目一新的」

senses.title: Again from the beginning; once more in a new way
senses.definition: starting again from the beginning, often after a failure or interruption
senses.definitionCN: 从起点再次出发，常发生在失败或中断之后
senses.example: After the project failed, the team decided to start afresh with a smaller plan.
senses.exampleCN: 项目失败后，团队决定用更小的方案从头再来。
senses.why: Fresh means new; adverbial a- plus fresh pictures wiping the board clean and acting as if nothing had been done yet.
senses.whyCN: fresh 意为「新鲜」；副词化的 a- + fresh 画出「擦净黑板、当作从未做过」的画面，即「从头再来」。

senses.title: In a new or different manner
senses.titleCN: 以新的方式；换一个角度
senses.definition: looking at or doing something as if for the first time, without the weight of habit
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛初次般地看待或处理事物，不受旧习惯的束缚
senses.example: The coach made the squad watch the match afresh, frame by frame.
senses.exampleCN: 教练让队员一帧一帧地重新审视整场比赛。
senses.why: Newness of method follows from newness of start: if you begin again, you may also see differently.
senses.whyCN: 既然可以重新开始，自然也可以换新眼光；「新的起点」顺势长出「新的方式」一义。

senses.title: With renewed freshness or energy
senses.titleCN: 精神焕发地；重新恢复活力
senses.definition: with energy or interest restored, as if refreshed
senses.definitionCN: 精力或兴致得到恢复，仿佛焕然一新
senses.example: She returned from holiday able to face the work afresh.
senses.exampleCN: 休假归来，她又能精神饱满地投入工作了。
senses.why: Fresh also means lively and unworn; when rest restores that quality, activity resumes afresh.
senses.whyCN: fresh 也有「精神饱满、未见磨损」之意；当休整找回这种状态，行动便「焕然一新地」重新开始。

intro.en: A native English adverb: the prefix a- plus fresh, first recorded in late Middle English.
intro.cn: 英语本土副词：前缀 a- + fresh，最早见于晚期中古英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *prewsk- (fresh, vigorous) underlies fresh and its Germanic cousins.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *prewsk-（新鲜、有活力）是 fresh 及其日耳曼同族词的远源。

items.en: fresc meant fresh, vigorous, not salted (of water).
items.cn: 古英语 fresc 意为「新鲜的、有生气的，（水）淡的」。

items.en: fresh was widespread; the a- prefix began attaching to adjectives to make state adverbs.
items.cn: 中古英语中 fresh 已很常用；前缀 a- 开始附着于形容词构成状态副词。

items.en: afresh appears with the sense of again, anew, first in religious and moral writing.
items.cn: afresh 以「重新、再」之义出现，最早见于宗教与训诫文字。

items.en: The collocation start afresh anchors the word; other uses follow the pattern of new beginnings.
items.cn: 现代英语中 start afresh 是锚定搭配，其余用法都围绕「新起点」展开。

note.en: Afresh stresses newness of start; again is neutral and anew is literary.
note.cn: afresh 强调「重新」中的新意；again 中性，anew 偏书面。

entries.definitionCN: 湿壁画——意大利语借词，同源远亲（意「新鲜的」灰泥），但指画作

entries.definition: burning; glowing with emotion
entries.definitionCN: 燃烧着；激动的——同款 a- 前缀构词

entries.definition: from the beginning, from scratch

entries.definition: to do it over: do it again from the start

entries.definition: both mean starting again; afresh adds the flavour of freshness

normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 a + fresh：再来一次，像新的一样。

normal.en: start afresh is the anchor phrase: begin from zero
normal.cn: start afresh 是锚定搭配：从零开始

normal.en: afresh = again + fresh: repeat, but with newness
normal.cn: afresh ＝ again（再）+ fresh（新），重复中带着新意

normal.en: look at it afresh: see it as if for the first time
normal.cn: look at it afresh：像第一次见到那样去看

normal.en: afire, afoot, afresh: the a- family again
normal.cn: afire、afoot、afresh：又一个 a- 家族成员

normal.en: refresh versus afresh: refresh restores you, afresh restarts the task
normal.cn: refresh 恢复的是人，afresh 重启的是事

abstract.en: A blank canvas after the failed painting is scraped off
abstract.cn: 失败的画被刮掉后，画布重新变白

abstract.en: Morning mist lifting so the same street looks brand new
abstract.cn: 晨雾散去，同一条街道焕然如新

abstract.en: A game board reset, pieces back on the starting squares
abstract.cn: 棋盘重摆，棋子回到各自的起点

examples.en: The editor threw out the draft and wrote the opening afresh.
examples.cn: 编辑推翻草稿，重写开篇。

examples.en: Every spring the garden seems to come alive afresh.
examples.cn: 每逢春天，花园都仿佛重新苏醒。

examples.en: The court ordered the case to be heard afresh.
examples.cn: 法院下令此案重新审理。

sensesIntro.en: From fresh-as-new grows the sense of starting over, seeing anew, and returning with restored energy.

branches.cn: 失败或中断之后从头再来

branches.en: repetition that carries newness
branches.cn: 带着新意的重复

definition_zh: 事后想起的想法；事后的补充
definition_en: an idea or addition that occurs to someone only after the main action or statement is finished
core_image: 关门后拍额头：事情办完才想起漏了的话
scene: 邮件发出去两分钟后，她才想起忘了问时间。She asked about the venue first and mentioned the dress code as an afterthought.
sceneCN: 这里 afterthought 是「事后的补充」（第 1 个义项：主事完成后才想起补上的想法）；句意是她先问了地点，末了才顺口补了句着装要求。

pos.zh: 事后想起的想法；事后补充

collocations.zh: 安全被当作事后才考虑的事

derivatives.zh: 组合词的前半部分，义为「在……之后」
组合词的后半部分，think 的名词形式，义为「想法；思考」
同构词的镜像词，义为「先见；预先考虑」

senses.title: An idea occurring after the event
senses.titleCN: 事后想起的想法；事后补充
senses.definition: a remark or item added when the main part is already done, showing it was not planned in advance
senses.definitionCN: 主要部分完成之后才补上的一句话或一项内容，说明事先并未计划
senses.example: She asked about the venue first and mentioned the dress code as an afterthought.
senses.exampleCN: 她先问了地点，末了才顺口补了句着装要求。
senses.why: The compound is literal: a thought that arrives after. Its core image is the missed item remembered too late.
senses.whyCN: 复合词结构即字面义：「之后」才到来的「想法」；核心画面是事过之后才想起的遗漏。

senses.title: Something given too little and too late
senses.titleCN: 不被重视的次要事物；临时敷衍的添加
senses.definition: something added carelessly at the end and treated as unimportant
senses.definitionCN: 末尾随手加上、被当作无关紧要的东西
senses.example: Accessibility was an afterthought in the design, bolted on at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 无障碍设计在这套方案里只是事后补丁，最后一刻才草草加上。
senses.why: Because an afterthought was never planned, it is by definition second-class; the word turned that defect into a criticism.
senses.whyCN: 既然是「事后才想起」，就注定不是重点；词义由此转出批评色彩——「敷衍的、次要的添加」。

intro.en: A transparent English compound of after plus thought, modelled on earlier after-words.
intro.cn: 一目了然的英语复合词：after（之后）+ thought（想法），仿照更早的 after- 系词构成。

items.en: The root *terk- (to twist, to form) is generally linked to think and thought.
items.cn: 一般认为 think / thought 与重构词根 *terk-（搓转、成形）相关。

items.en: after and þoht existed separately; compounds with after- named whatever followed.
items.cn: 古英语中 after 与 þoht 各自独立；after- 系复合词命名「随后出现的事物」。

items.en: afterthought appears in the sense of later reflection, sometimes regret.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 afterthought，意为「事后的思索」，有时带悔意。

items.en: The sense settled on an addition made afterwards, often contrasted with forethought.
items.cn: 十七至十八世纪词义固定为「事后添加」，常与 forethought（预先考虑）相对。

items.en: The phrase as an afterthought is idiomatic; the word often criticises neglected priorities.
items.cn: 现代英语中 as an afterthought 已成语化；该词常用于批评被忽视的优先事项。

note.en: Afterthought is the mirror of forethought; it differs from a simple addition by arriving late and unplanned.
note.cn: afterthought 与 forethought 互为镜像；它与普通的「补充」不同，在于来得晚且不在计划内。

entries.definition: planning or care for the future in advance
entries.definitionCN: 先见；预先考虑——同构词的镜像词

entries.definition: a delayed result of an action
entries.definitionCN: 后效；后遗症——同为 after- 复合词

entries.definition: not considering others; careless

entries.definition: life after death

entries.definition: an item added to a document afterwards

entries.definition: a note added after the main text, as in a letter

entries.definition: looking back on past events

entries.definition: understanding of events only after they happen
entries.definitionCN: 事后聪明；后见之明——认知层面的事后之见

entries.definition: advance planning
entries.definitionCN: 预先考虑——afterthought 的反义镜像

normalIntro.en: Read the compound literally: a thought that comes after.
normalIntro.cn: 按字面拆读：after（之后）+ thought（想法）＝ 之后才来的想法。

normal.en: after + thought: the idea arrived too late
normal.cn: after + thought：想法来得太迟

normal.en: as an afterthought is the fixed phrase: tacked on at the end
normal.cn: as an afterthought 是固定搭配：末尾随手补上一句

normal.en: afterthought versus forethought: too late versus just in time
normal.cn: afterthought（事后才想）对照 forethought（提前想到）

normal.en: safety as an afterthought: criticism of neglected priorities
normal.cn: safety as an afterthought 批评「安全成了事后才考虑的事」

normal.en: postscript is its cousin in letters: both arrive after the main text

abstract.en: A ramp bolted onto a finished staircase

examples.en: The greenhouse looked like an afterthought, squeezed between garage and fence.
examples.cn: 那间温室像是事后加盖的，挤在车库和栅栏之间。

examples.en: He apologized for forgetting her birthday, calling it a terrible lapse rather than an afterthought.
examples.cn: 他为忘记她的生日道歉，说这是严重疏忽，并非事后才想起。

examples.en: User privacy should never be an afterthought in app design.
examples.cn: 在应用设计中，用户隐私绝不应是事后才想起的补丁。

definition_en: with the mouth wide open, especially in surprise; wide open

scene: 魔术师掀开斗篷的瞬间，全场的孩子都看呆了。The children watched agape as the magician pulled a rabbit from his empty hat.

senses.title: With the mouth wide open in wonder or surprise
senses.definition: staring with the mouth open because of amazement or shock
senses.definitionCN: 因惊异或震惊而张着嘴凝视
senses.example: The children watched agape as the magician pulled a rabbit from his empty hat.
senses.exampleCN: 魔术师从空帽子里拽出兔子时，孩子们张着嘴看呆了。
senses.why: The state prefix a- fixes the verb gape into an image: the mouth held open by astonishment.
senses.whyCN: 状态前缀 a- 把动词 gape 凝固成画面：嘴巴被惊讶「挂」在张开的位置。

senses.title: Wide open, of things
senses.definition: of a mouth, door, or crack, standing wide open
senses.definitionCN: 形容嘴、门、裂缝等大敞着
senses.example: The elevator doors stood agape, revealing an empty shaft.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯门大敞着，露出空空的井道。
senses.why: Anything that gapes shares the image of an opening held wide, so the adjective extends from faces to doors and fissures.
senses.whyCN: 凡是「张大」的东西都共享「敞开的口」这一意象，形容词义便从人脸延伸到门缝与裂口。

intro.en: The prefix a- plus the verb gape; a native formation, reinforced in form by Greek agape (love), with which it is unrelated.
intro.cn: 前缀 a- 加动词 gape 构成，属英语本土构词；其拼写恰与希腊语 agape（圣爱）相同，但二者毫无关联。

items.en: The reconstructed root *gheh- (to yawn, to open wide) underlies gape, gap, and yawn.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *gheh-（打哈欠、张大）是 gape、gap、yawn 的共同远源。

items.en: gap meant a chasm; the verb gapa meant to open the mouth.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 gap 意为「裂口」，动词 gapa 意为「张嘴」。

items.en: gape was borrowed and soon native; gap split off as a separate noun.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 gape 并迅速本土化；gap 另立为独立名词。

items.en: The state form agape developed, describing mouths held open in wonder.
items.cn: 十五至十七世纪产生状态化形式 agape，描写因惊异而大张的嘴。

items.en: Agape now almost always implies astonishment; the plain open sense survives in literary use.
items.cn: 现代英语中 agape 几乎总含惊愕义；单纯的「敞开」义主要留在书面语。

note.en: Agape the state word must not be confused with Greek agape (divine love); note the different stress in careful speech.
note.cn: 状态词 agape 不可与希腊语借词 agape（圣爱）混淆；正式语境中二者重音不同。

entries.definition: selfless, divine love in Christian Greek

entries.definitionCN: 缺口；差距——同源名词，指「张开的空隙」

entries.definition: struck with horror or shock

sensesIntro.en: One image, two carriers: the astonished mouth and any opening held wide.

definition_zh: 使成团；聚集；团块；结块的
definition_en: to gather into a mass or cluster; a clustered mass; formed into a ball or heap
core_image: 滚雪球：碎屑越滚越大，粘成一团
scene: 山脚下，火山灰凝成了拳头大的石块。Ash fragments agglomerate into round stones as the volcano cools.
sceneCN: 这里 agglomerate 是「聚结成团」（第 1 个义项：散粒黏聚为一体）；句意是火山冷却时，灰烬碎屑聚结成圆石。

derivatives.zh: agglomerate 加名词后缀 -ion，义为「聚集（体）；集结」
同根拉丁 glomus 一支，义为「小球状聚伞花序」
同根加 con- 前缀，义为「混合聚集物；企业集团」

senses.title: To collect or form into a mass or ball
senses.definition: to gather scattered particles or things into one clustered mass
senses.definitionCN: 把分散的颗粒或事物黏聚成一个团块
senses.example: Ash fragments agglomerate into round stones as the volcano cools.
senses.exampleCN: 火山冷却时，灰烬碎屑聚结成圆石。
senses.why: The Latin root glomus means a ball of yarn; rolling loose threads into a ball is the exact image of gathering particles into a lump.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 glomus 意为「线团」；把散线滚成球，正是「碎粒聚成团块」的核心画面。

senses.title: A clustered mass, especially of rock or businesses
senses.definition: a mass of clustered fragments, or a group of firms or districts grown together
senses.definitionCN: 碎块聚成的团，或连成一片的企业群、城镇群
senses.example: The firm grew from a workshop into an agglomerate of fourteen brands.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司从一间作坊成长为拥有十四个品牌的联合体。
senses.why: Whatever particles do, institutions imitate: separate units fused into one body are a ball of yarn in the economic image.
senses.whyCN: 颗粒会成团，机构亦然：各自独立却熔为一体的单位，在经济图景里就是一个「线团」。

senses.title: Formed into a clustered mass
senses.definition: describing matter that has clumped together rather than staying dispersed
senses.definitionCN: 形容物质已结块抱团，而非保持分散
senses.example: Powder that has absorbed moisture becomes agglomerate and will not pour.
senses.exampleCN: 受潮的粉末会结成团，倒不出来了。
senses.why: The result state of the action becomes a property: once rolled into a ball, the material is simply agglomerate.
senses.whyCN: 动作的结果沉淀为属性：一旦滚成了球，这种材料就「是」结块的了。

intro.en: From Latin agglomerare (to wind into a ball), built on glomus (ball of yarn), through post-classical and scientific Latin into English.
intro.cn: 源自拉丁语 agglomerare「卷成球」，建立在 glomus（线团）之上，经近代学术拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The root *glem- (to stick, to smear) is reconstructed behind glomus and its cousins.
items.cn: 一般认为 glomus 及其同族词背后是重构词根 *glem-（粘、涂）。

items.en: glomus meant a ball of yarn; agglomerare meant to add to the ball, to wind on.
items.cn: 拉丁语 glomus 意为「线团」，agglomerare 意为「往球上绕、卷成一团」。

items.en: agglomeratus served in alchemy and early geology for fused lumps of matter.
items.cn: 近代拉丁语 agglomeratus 用于炼金术与早期地质学，指熔结的块状物。

items.en: Science adopted the verb for particles clustering, later for rocks and city growth.
items.cn: 十七至十九世纪科学界用其动词指颗粒结团，后扩展到岩石与城市扩张。

items.en: Today the word lives in geology, materials science, and economics of urban clusters.
items.cn: 如今该词活跃于地质学、材料科学和城市经济学的「集聚」语境。

note.en: Agglomerate stresses one coherent ball; agglomeration is looser, and conglomeration implies a mixed heap.
note.cn: agglomerate 强调凝成一个整体；agglomeration 较松散，conglomeration 则含「混杂堆聚」之意。

normal.cn: conglomeration 与 agglomeration 同根 glomer：前者杂凑，后者单纯聚集

abstract.cn: 雪球滚下山坡，越滚越肥

examples.cn: 淀粉颗粒受热遇潮会聚结，形成糊状。

examples.cn: 这家集团宣布合并，将把八家子公司聚为一体。

examples.en: Lava agglomerate was used to pave the old Roman road.
examples.cn: 古罗马大道用火山集块岩铺成。

sensesIntro.en: From rolling particles into a ball grow the mass noun, the fused institution, and the resulting state adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把碎粒滚成球」长出团块名词、机构融合义与结果状态形容词。

branches.cn: 碎粒被吸入同一团块

definition_zh: 扩大；增高（权力、地位）；抬高（自己）
definition_en: to increase the power, wealth, or rank of; to make oneself seem greater
core_image: 权力雪球：有人不断往自己的权杖上加码
scene: 总裁把同盟的部门逐一吞并，权柄日益膨胀。The CEO aggrandized his own office by absorbing every allied department.

pos.zh: 扩大；增高（权力、财富、地位）

senses.title: To make oneself seem or become greater
senses.definition: to give oneself more importance, often at others' expense
senses.definitionCN: 给自己增加重要性，常以牺牲他人为代价
senses.example: He tells war stories only to aggrandize himself before new hires.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲从前的光辉事迹，只为在新人面前抬高自己。
senses.why: The root grand means great; when the arrow of making-great turns back on the doer, self-importance is the result.
senses.whyCN: 词根 grand 意为「大」；当「使之变大」的箭头折回施动者自身，便长出「自我抬高」之义。

senses.title: To increase the power, wealth, or territory of a person or state
senses.definition: to enlarge the scope of someone's authority, riches, or dominion
senses.definitionCN: 扩大某人的职权、财富或统治范围
senses.example: The CEO aggrandized his own office by absorbing every allied department.
senses.exampleCN: 总裁通过吞并所有盟友部门来不断扩充自己的职权。
senses.why: This is the historical core: crowns and estates grew the way a snowball does, by adding everything nearby.
senses.whyCN: 这是词义的历史核心：王权与领地像雪球一样，靠不断吞并周围的一切而增大。

intro.en: From French agrandir, built on grand (great), remodelled with the Latin-looking ending -ize in English.
intro.cn: 源自法语 agrandir（使变大），建立在 grand（大）之上；英语中又按拉丁词形改写成 -ize 结尾。

items.en: grandis meant great, large; it gave Old French grand.
items.cn: 拉丁语 grandis 意为「大的、宏伟的」，派生古法语 grand。

items.en: agrandir meant to make greater, to enlarge.
items.cn: 古法语 agrandir 意为「使变大；扩大」。

items.en: Borrowed as aggradeise and reshaped to aggrandize with the productive -ize ending.
items.cn: 十六世纪借入英语，初作 aggradeise，后依 -ize 后缀改写为 aggrandize。

items.en: Applied to crowns, estates, and offices; the reflexive self-aggrandizing use grew alongside.
items.cn: 用于王权、地产与官职；「自我膨胀」的反身用法随之发展。

items.en: Now often pejorative: self-aggrandizement names vain self-promotion.
items.cn: 如今常带贬义：self-aggrandizement 指虚荣的自我抬举。

note.en: Aggrandize belongs to the grand family; its near neighbours all describe enlargement, but with different materials.
note.cn: aggrandize 属 grand 词族；近邻词都表「扩大」，但扩张的对象各异。

entries.definition: to raise in rank or praise highly

entries.definition: to spread out or increase in size

entries.definitionCN: 贬低；轻视——aggrandize 的反义

normal.cn: ag+grand+ize：让某人变得「宏大」

normal.cn: self-aggrandizing 是常见的批评用语：自我膨胀的

normal.cn: grandeur、grandiose、aggrandize 同属「大」的家族

normal.cn: aggravate 拼写相近但义为「恶化」，不是「扩大」

normal.en: aggrandize one's power: snowball the authority
normal.cn: aggrandize one's power：像滚雪球一样累积权柄

abstract.cn: 王座不断垫高，直至俯瞰整个大厅

examples.cn: 批评者说，那座纪念碑纯粹是为了给独裁者抬轿撑场面。

examples.en: The dynasty aggrandized its realm through three centuries of treaties and wars.

definition_zh: 恶化；加重；恼怒；烦躁
definition_en: the act of making something worse; a feeling of annoyance
core_image: 压在伤腿上的另一块石头：本已不堪，还要加码
scene: 雨越下越大，屋顶的漏洞让霉斑迅速蔓延。The aggravation of the damp problem forced the family to move out.
sceneCN: 这里 aggravation 是「恶化、加重」（第 1 个义项：状况变得更糟）；句意是潮湿问题不断恶化，一家人不得不搬走。

senses.title: The act of making a condition worse
senses.definition: the process of increasing the seriousness of an illness, problem, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病、问题或局势的严重程度上升的过程
senses.example: The aggravation of the damp problem forced the family to move out.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿问题不断恶化，一家人不得不搬走。
senses.why: The Latin root gravis means heavy; aggravation is literally adding weight to what already presses down.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 gravis 意为「重」；aggravation 的本义就是往已经很沉的东西上再加砝码。

senses.title: A feeling of annoyance or exasperation
senses.definition: a state of being irritated, especially by repeated small troubles
senses.definitionCN: 被激怒的状态，尤指被反复的小麻烦磨出来的火气
senses.example: Every phone call with the insurer is pure aggravation.
senses.exampleCN: 每次和保险公司通电话都是纯粹的煎熬。
senses.why: In American colloquial speech, adding weight to the mind became adding irritation, so the emotional sense split off.
senses.whyCN: 美式口语把「给心灵加压」转成「添堵」，于是从「加重」义分岔出「恼怒、烦躁」的情绪义。

intro.en: From Latin aggravatio, built on gravis (heavy); the legal sense of worsening an offence came first, the emotional sense much later.
intro.cn: 源自拉丁语 aggravatio，建立在 gravis（重）之上；先有「罪行加重」的法律义，「恼怒」的口语义出现很晚。

items.en: The root *gwere- (heavy) underlies gravis, grave, and grief.
items.cn: 重构词根 *gwere-（重）是 gravis、grave 与 grief 的共同远源。

items.en: gravis meant heavy; aggravare meant to make heavier.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gravis 意为「重的」，aggravare 意为「使更重」。

items.en: aggravatio named the heightening of a charge's seriousness in Roman law.
items.cn: 法律拉丁语中 aggravatio 指加重罪行的严重程度。

items.en: Borrowed for the worsening of diseases and offences; aggravated burglary survives in law.
items.cn: 借入英语后用于病情与罪行的加重；aggravated burglary 至今仍是法律用语。

items.en: Colloquial American use shifted the word to mean provocation and annoyance.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪美式口语转向「挑衅、惹恼」，情绪义由此确立。

note.en: Aggravation spans the heavy family of grave and grief; annoyance names the feeling without the added weight.
note.cn: aggravation 连着 grave、grief 的「沉重」词族；annoyance 只指情绪，不含「雪上加霜」之意。

definition_zh: 侵略；攻击；挑衅
definition_en: to make an attack or begin a quarrel; to commit aggression
core_image: 先迈出的一步：越过界线向别人逼近
scene: 哨卡前，对面的巡逻队又朝我方边界逼近。The patrol began to aggress across the border at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 aggress 是「侵犯、进犯」（第 1 个义项：率先发起攻击、越过边界）；句意是对方巡逻队黎明时分开始越界进犯。

derivatives.zh: aggress 加名词后缀 -ion，义为「侵略；攻击性」

senses.title: To launch an attack or invasion first
senses.definition: to begin hostilities by attacking another party or crossing a boundary
senses.definitionCN: 通过攻击他方或越界而率先挑起敌对行动
senses.example: The patrol began to aggress across the border at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 对方巡逻队黎明时分开始越界进犯。
senses.why: The Latin gradus is a step; to aggress is to take the first hostile step toward the other side.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 gradus 意为「步子」；aggress 就是朝着对方先迈出的敌意一步。

senses.title: To encroach upon rights or interests
senses.definition: to intrude on someone's rights, space, or interests
senses.definitionCN: 侵害他人的权利、领域或利益
senses.example: The new clause could aggress upon tenants' long-standing rights.
senses.exampleCN: 新条款可能侵害租户长期享有的权利。
senses.why: A hostile step need not be military; any advance over a boundary, even a legal one, keeps the image.
senses.whyCN: 敌意的一步不必是军事的；任何越界推进——哪怕只发生在法律文本里——都保留了这一画面。

intro.en: From Latin aggredi (to approach, to attack), built on gradus (step), via French aggredir into English.
intro.cn: 源自拉丁语 aggredi「逼近、攻击」，建立在 gradus（步子）之上，经法语 aggredir 进入英语。

items.en: The root *ghredh- (to walk, to go) underlies gradus and its large family.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ghredh-（行走）是 gradus 及其庞大家族的远源。

items.en: aggredi meant to walk toward, to set upon; the noun aggressio named an attack.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aggredi 意为「走向、扑向」，名词 aggressio 即「攻击」。

items.en: aggression and aggredir kept the sense of initiating an attack.
items.cn: 法语的 aggression 与 aggredir 保留「率先攻击」之义。

items.en: aggress entered as a formal verb; aggression soon eclipsed it in ordinary use.
items.cn: aggress 以正式动词身份进入英语；普通用法很快被 aggression 压过。

items.en: The bare verb is now rare and legal or rhetorical; its derivatives dominate.
items.cn: 如今裸动词罕见，多见于法律或修辞；占主导地位的是它的派生词。

note.en: Aggress is the bare verb beneath a famous family: aggression, aggressive, aggressor.
note.cn: aggress 是一个著名词族下的裸动词：aggression、aggressive、aggressor 皆由此而来。
