senses.title: Ready to attack or fight
senses.definition: ready to attack, fight, or argue, and likely to do so at small provocation
senses.definitionCN: 随时准备攻击、打斗或争吵，一点刺激就会发作
senses.example: The dog becomes aggressive whenever strangers come near its food.
senses.exampleCN: 一有陌生人靠近它的食物，这条狗就变得凶起来。
senses.why: This is the adjective's oldest layer: a person or animal whose first response to a threat is to step forward rather than back away.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个形容词最古老的一层：面对威胁时，人或动物的第一反应是上前一步，而不是退开。

senses.title: Forceful in pursuit of success
senses.definition: very determined and forceful in pursuing goals, especially in business or sport
senses.definitionCN: 为实现目标而十分坚定、强硬，尤用于商业或体育
senses.example: They took an aggressive approach to winning new customers.
senses.exampleCN: 他们采取了强势的做法去争取新客户。
senses.why: Business took the same forward push and removed the hostility: the energy is kept, the enemy is replaced by a target.
senses.whyCN: 商业沿用了同一个「向前顶」的动作，却去掉了敌意：劲头还在，敌人换成了目标。

senses.title: Unusually strong in method
senses.definition: unusually strong or severe in method, often used when a quick result matters more than caution
senses.definitionCN: 手段上异常强烈或猛烈，通常用于求快而不惜冒险的场合
senses.example: Doctors chose aggressive treatment because the tumour was growing fast.
senses.exampleCN: 因为肿瘤长得很快，医生选择了激进的治疗方案。
senses.why: Here the force is turned on a problem rather than a person, so the word means intense method rather than ill will.
senses.whyCN: 这里的力量是对着问题使的，不是对着人，所以这个词指的是手段猛烈，而非心怀恶意。

senses.title: Spreading fast, of a disease
senses.definition: of a disease, spreading quickly and hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病扩散迅速、难以控制
senses.example: This is an aggressive form of cancer that needs immediate surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一种侵袭性很强的癌症，需要立刻手术。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word for a growth that behaves like an attacker: it advances quickly and will not be held back.
senses.whyCN: 医学借这个词形容一种像入侵者那样行事的病变：推进快，而且拦不住。

intro.en: Aggressive is the adjective of the same Latin family as aggression: stepping towards someone with force.
intro.cn: aggressive 与 aggression 同属一个拉丁词族，本义是带着力量朝某人迈过去。

items.en: Gradi meant 'to step, walk', the base of a small family that includes gradient and graduate.
items.cn: gradi 意为「迈步、行走」，是包含 gradient、graduate 的小词族的根基。

items.en: ad- 'towards' plus gradi gave aggredi, 'to step towards', and in military use 'to attack'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 gradi 构成 aggredi，意为「朝……迈步」，军事用法中即「进攻」。

items.en: The late Latin adjective aggressivus described someone inclined to attack; it is recorded mainly in glosses.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语形容词 aggressivus 形容倾向于攻击的人，主要见于词表与注释。

items.en: English adopted aggressive first in the plain hostile sense, applied to persons and to states.
items.cn: 英语最初以直白的敌对义采用 aggressive，用于人与国家。

items.en: The business sense of 'forceful, go-getting' is a twentieth-century development, and the medical sense followed.
items.cn: 「强势、有闯劲」的商业义是二十世纪的发展，医学义随后出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the rest of the gradi family; the near-meaning group gathers words for force, each with a different target.
note.cn: 形近组收 gradi 词族的其余成员；近义组收表示「强硬」的词，区别在于力量对着什么使。

entries.definition: The noun for an attack or hostile behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 表示攻击行为或敌意的名词。

entries.definition: The one who attacks first.
entries.definitionCN: 先发动攻击的一方。

entries.definition: The rare verb meaning to attack.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的动词，意为攻击。

entries.definition: Unfriendly and ready to oppose, but not necessarily violent.
entries.definitionCN: 不友好、随时准备对抗，但不一定动手。

entries.definition: Strong and confident in making a point or pushing a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 表达观点或推行计划时有力而自信。

entries.definition: Standing up for oneself calmly, without attacking others.
entries.definitionCN: 平静地维护自己，而不攻击他人。

normalIntro.en: Four real parts carry the word: ad-, gradi, the assimilated g, and the adjective ending -ive.
normalIntro.cn: 四个真实部件承载这个词：ad-、gradi、被同化的 g，以及形容词词尾 -ive。

normal.en: Aggressive keeps the stepping root of aggression and adds -ive, so it means tending to step at people.
normal.cn: aggressive 保留 aggression 的「迈步」词根，加上 -ive，意为「动不动就朝人迈步」。

normal.en: A bull lowers its head and goes straight: that is the picture behind the word.
normal.cn: 公牛低下头、直直冲过去——这就是这个词背后的画面。

normal.en: The same energy is praise in sales and blame in traffic: context decides whether the force is admired.
normal.cn: 同一股劲头，在销售里是褒，在交通里是贬；是正是邪由语境决定。

normal.en: Aggressive does not take -er: use more and most before it.
normal.cn: aggressive 不加 -er：比较级和最高级用 more 与 most。

normal.en: Note the double g and the single s: ag-gress-ive.
normal.cn: 注意双 g 与单 s：ag-gress-ive。

abstract.en: Force is neutral until we ask who it is aimed at: at a person it is aggression, at a goal it is drive.
abstract.cn: 力量本身是中性的，要问它对着谁：对着人是攻击性，对着目标是闯劲。

abstract.en: A word that can praise and condemn at once shows how much of meaning is carried by context rather than by the root.
abstract.cn: 一个词能同时用来夸奖和指责，说明意义有多少是由语境而非词根承担的。

abstract.en: Calling a disease aggressive grants it a will, because the word was built for creatures that choose to advance.
abstract.cn: 把疾病称作 aggressive，等于赋予它意志，因为这个词本是为会主动进攻的生灵而造的。

examples.en: Some birds become aggressive when their nests are approached.
examples.cn: 有些鸟在巢被人靠近时会变得凶猛。

examples.en: The firm's aggressive pricing forced smaller rivals out of the market.
examples.cn: 这家公司的激进定价把较小的对手挤出了市场。

examples.en: She was aggressive in the interview but never rude.
examples.cn: 她在面试中很有冲劲，但从不失礼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额个雷死我」——额，那个冲过来的家伙差点把我撞死，太有攻击性了。

root: 源自拉丁语 aggredi「朝……迈步、进攻」，由 ad-「朝向」与 gradi「迈步」构成，加形容词后缀 -ive 表示「倾向于」如此。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses share one forward push: at a person it is hostility, at a target it is drive, at a problem it is intense method, and in a body it is a fast-spreading growth.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项共用同一个「向前顶」：对着人是敌意，对着目标是闯劲，对着难题是猛药，对着身体则是扩散很快的病变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bull lowers its head and drives straight ahead, seeing nothing on either side.
core.cn: 核心意象：公牛低下头，直直向前顶，两边什么也看不见。

branches.en: a dog that lunges at anyone near its bowl
branches.cn: 谁靠近食盆就扑上去的狗

branches.en: a sales team that calls first and calls again
branches.cn: 先打电话、再打第二次的销售团队

branches.en: a course of treatment stronger than usual
branches.cn: 比常规更猛的一轮治疗

branches.en: a tumour that spreads before it is found
branches.cn: 还没被发现就已经扩散的肿瘤

branches.en: one pushing force, blamed or praised by its target
branches.cn: 同一股向前的力，因对象不同而被贬或被褒

intro.en: A Latin verb of stepping, the prefix that aims it, and the adjective endings that build the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「迈步」的拉丁动词、给它定方向的前缀，以及构成这一词族的形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: gradi and aggressivus are recorded Latin; only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: gradi 与 aggressivus 都是有文献记录的拉丁词，只有更早的印欧词根属重构。

definition_zh: 使委屈；使愤愤不平；侵害
definition_en: to cause someone to feel wronged; to infringe upon someone's rights
core_image: 不公平的秤：被压低的那端满脸不平
scene: 评奖结果公布，落选的老员工满腹委屈。The opaque review process aggrieved many senior staff.
sceneCN: 这里 aggrieve 是「使委屈、使不平」（第 1 个义项：让人感到受了不公正对待）；句意是黑箱的考核流程让许多资深员工愤愤不平。

pos.zh: 使委屈；使愤愤不平；侵害

derivatives.zh: aggrieve 的过去分词形容词化，义为「愤愤不平的；受委屈的」
同根法语分支名词，义为「悲痛」
同根动词，义为「使悲伤；哀悼」
grieve 加名词后缀 -ance，义为「不满；申诉」

senses.title: To make someone feel wronged or resentful
senses.definition: to treat a person so unfairly that resentment follows
senses.definitionCN: 以不公正的方式对待某人，使其心生怨恨
senses.example: The opaque review process aggrieved many senior staff.
senses.exampleCN: 黑箱的考核流程让许多资深员工愤愤不平。
senses.why: The Latin gravis is weight; unfairness loads an invisible weight on a person, and the mind bows under grievance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 gravis 意为「重」；不公等于往人身上压一副看不见的重担，心情便在委屈下弯了腰。

senses.title: To infringe upon someone's rights
senses.definition: to violate or injure a person's legal rights or interests
senses.definitionCN: 侵犯或损害某人的法定权利与利益
senses.example: The council's ruling aggrieved the property owners' title.
senses.exampleCN: 议会的裁决损害了业主的产权。
senses.why: Law formalised the weight image: whoever loads the burden on another has aggrieved that party in the eyes of the court.
senses.whyCN: 法律把「压重担」的画面制度化：谁把担子压到别人身上，谁就在法庭眼中 aggrieve 了对方。

intro.en: From Old French agrever, from Latin aggravare (to make heavy), with the vowel reshaped by folk link to grief.
intro.cn: 源自古法语 agrever，出自拉丁语 aggravare「使沉重」；因民间联想 grief 而改换了元音拼写。

items.en: The root *gwere- (heavy) is shared by gravis, grave, grief, and aggrieve.
items.cn: 词根 *gwere-（重）为 gravis、grave、grief 与 aggrieve 所共享。

items.en: aggravare meant to weigh down, to make heavier.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aggravare 意为「压重；使更沉重」。

items.en: agrever kept the sense of burdening or wronging someone.
items.cn: 古法语 agrever 保留「使负累、使受屈」之义。

items.en: aggrever named the infringement of rights in petitions and pleas.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-诺曼法律文书中 aggrever 指「侵害权利」。

items.en: aggrieve entered English with both the emotional and the legal senses; aggrieved later became the common adjective.
items.cn: 十三世纪起 aggrieve 进入英语，兼有情绪义与法律义；形容词 aggrieved 后来成为常用形式。

note.en: Aggrieve sits in the heavy family of grief; wronged names the state without naming the burden.
note.cn: aggrieve 属 grief 的「沉重」词族；wronged 只描述状态，不含「重担」意象。

entries.definition: to feel deep sorrow
entries.definitionCN: 悲痛；哀悼——同根，重担化为哀伤

entries.definition: a complaint about unfair treatment
entries.definitionCN: 不满；申诉——aggrieve 的结果名词

entries.definition: feeling wronged
entries.definitionCN: 愤愤不平的——最常用的派生形式

entries.definition: to make worse
entries.definitionCN: 使恶化——拉丁同源孪生词，拼写更接近原形

entries.definition: to treat unjustly
entries.definitionCN: 冤枉；不公对待——最平实的近义动词

entries.definition: to harm, including in law
entries.definitionCN: 伤害；法律上指损害（权利）

entries.definition: to soothe anger
entries.definitionCN: 安抚——aggrieve 的情绪反义

entries.definition: to feel bitter about
entries.definitionCN: 怨恨——描述 aggrieve 造成的心理结果

normalIntro.en: See grieve inside the word: aggrieve is what others do to make you grieve.
normalIntro.cn: 在词里看见 grieve：aggrieve 就是让别人「伤心、憋屈」的行为。

normal.en: ag + grieve: load grief onto someone
normal.cn: ag + grieve：把委屈压到别人身上

normal.en: feel aggrieved is the standard passive-feeling phrase
normal.cn: feel aggrieved 是标准搭配：感到受了委屈

normal.en: an aggrieved party: legal phrase for the wronged side
normal.cn: an aggrieved party 是法律用语：受害一方

normal.en: grievance, grieve, aggrieved: one heavy family
normal.cn: grievance、grieve、aggrieved 同属「沉重」家族

normal.en: aggrieve versus aggravate: wrong a person versus worsen a thing
normal.cn: aggrieve 委屈的是人，aggravate 加重的是事

abstract.en: A scale tipped by hidden stones against one side
abstract.cn: 天平被暗藏的石块压向一侧

abstract.en: A person carrying a rucksack of someone else's mistakes
abstract.cn: 一个人背着装满他人过错的登山包

abstract.en: A door prize handed to everyone except the one who waited longest
abstract.cn: 奖品人人有份，唯独跳过等得最久的那位

examples.en: Tenants felt aggrieved when the rules changed without notice.
examples.cn: 规则说改就改、事先不打招呼，租户们都觉得受了委屈。

examples.en: The appellate court held that the statute aggrieved the plaintiffs' due-process rights.
examples.cn: 上诉法院认定该法规侵害了原告的正当程序权利。

examples.en: He spoke in an aggrieved tone, listing every small slight he remembered.
examples.cn: 他用委屈的语气历数自己记得的每一次冷遇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额·跪夫」——委屈得额都青了，几乎要向人下跪。谐音仅助记，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ gravis（重的）构成 aggravare「压重」，经古法语 agrever 进入英语作 aggrieve，拼写受 grief 类推影响；「往人身上压重担」即「使受屈、侵害其权利」。

sensesIntro.en: One burden, two verdicts: the wounded heart and the violated right.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一副重担，两处裁定：受伤的心与被侵犯的权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unfair scale pressing one side down
core.cn: 核心意象：把一端压低的不公平天平

branches.en: injustice felt in the heart
branches.cn: 心中感受到的不公

branches.en: burden laid on someone by another
branches.cn: 由他人压来的重担

branches.en: rights violated in court's eyes
branches.cn: 法庭眼中被侵犯的权利

branches.en: the basis of a formal complaint
branches.cn: 正式申诉的依据

branches.en: the tone of the person wronged
branches.cn: 受屈者特有的语气

intro.en: The word combines ag- (ad-) with the grav root, its spelling softened toward grief.
intro.cn: 该词由前缀 ag-（即 ad-）加 grav 词根构成，拼写向 grief 靠拢。

latinIntro.en: The grav family links heaviness, seriousness, sorrow, and injury.
latinIntro.cn: grav 词族把沉重、严重、悲伤与侵害串成一线。

items.exampleCN: aggrieve、aggravate 中 g 前的 ad- 均写作 ag-
严重身体伤害（法律用语）

latinEntries.exampleCN: 整个词族的根源

latinEntries.example: source of aggrieve and aggravate alike
latinEntries.exampleCN: aggrieve 与 aggravate 的共同来源

derivatives.zh: 愤愤不平的；受屈的（aggrieve 的分词形容词）
不满；申诉（同根名词）
极严重的；悲痛的（同根形容词）

definition_zh: 惊骇的；吓呆的
definition_en: struck with shock, horror, or amazement
core_image: 血一下子凉透：惊吓从脚底窜上头顶
scene: 拆开信封，账单上的数字让他僵在原地。He stood aghast at the sum on the final bill.
sceneCN: 这里 aghast 是「惊骇的」（第 1 个义项：被吓到失语僵立）；句意是看到最终账单上的金额，他惊得僵在原地。

pos.zh: 惊骇的；吓呆的（表语用法）

derivatives.zh: 同源日耳曼词 gast 的一支，义为「鬼魂」
ghost 同族形容词，义为「可怕的；苍白的」
aghast 加后缀 -ly（旧式罕用），义为「惊骇地」

senses.title: Struck with shock or horror
senses.definition: filled with sudden shock or terror, often shown by a frozen stare
senses.definitionCN: 充满突如其来的震惊或恐惧，常表现为僵住的凝视
senses.example: He stood aghast at the sum on the final bill.
senses.exampleCN: 看到最终账单上的金额，他惊得僵在原地。
senses.why: The Old English gast meant spirit or breath; to be aghast was to have the breath frightened out of you.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gast 意为「气息、灵魂」；aghast 的本义就是「被吓得魂飞魄散、气息全无」。

senses.title: Filled with horror at something seen as wrong
senses.titleCN: 对（不义之事）深感震惊的
senses.definition: shocked by something considered outrageous or unacceptable
senses.definitionCN: 对被视为恶劣或不可接受之事感到震惊
senses.example: Readers were aghast that the prize went to a plagiarist.
senses.exampleCN: 奖项颁给了剽窃者，读者们惊骇不已。
senses.why: Horror at danger widened to moral shock: the same frozen breath meets a villain as a ghost.
senses.whyCN: 对危险的恐惧扩大为道义上的震惊：面对恶行与面对鬼魂，同样吓得倒抽冷气。

intro.en: From the past participle of agasten (to frighten), built on Old English gāst (spirit, ghost).
intro.cn: 源自动词 agasten「吓唬」的过去分词，建立在古英语 gāst（灵魂、鬼魂）之上。

items.en: The root *gheys- (to be excited, frightened) underlies gast and ghost.
items.cn: 一般认为词根 *gheys-（激动、惊惧）是 gast 与 ghost 的远源。

items.en: gāst meant breath, spirit, ghost; the verb agāstan meant to terrify.
items.cn: 古英语 gāst 意为「气息、灵魂、鬼魂」，动词 agāstan 意为「使恐惧」。

items.en: agast served as the past participle: frightened out of one's wits.
items.cn: 中古英语 agast 用作过去分词：「被吓得魂不附体」。

items.en: Spelling settled as aghast under the influence of ghost.
items.cn: 十五至十六世纪拼写受 ghost 影响定型为 aghast。

items.en: Now almost purely predicative: stand aghast, be aghast at.
items.cn: 如今几乎只作表语：stand aghast、be aghast at。

note.en: Aghast names the frozen face of horror; appalled adds moral outrage, horrified adds fear.
note.cn: aghast 刻画惊骇时僵住的脸；appalled 多一层道义愤怒，horrified 多一层恐惧。

entries.definition: the spirit of a dead person
entries.definitionCN: 鬼魂——同源词，aghast 的吓人源头

entries.definition: frightful, dreadful
entries.definitionCN: 可怕的；苍白的——同族形容词

entries.definition: with the mouth wide open
entries.definitionCN: 目瞪口呆地——同为 a- 系状态词，情绪相邻

entries.definition: aghast is standard; aghastly is archaic
entries.definitionCN: aghast 是标准形；aghastly 已成古旧用法

entries.definition: shocked and disgusted
entries.definitionCN: 惊骇且愤慨的

entries.definition: filled with horror
entries.definitionCN: 惊恐的

entries.definition: struck speechless by shock
entries.definitionCN: 惊得说不出话的——与「气息被吓跑」意象呼应

entries.definition: calm, not disturbed
entries.definitionCN: 镇定的——aghast 的反面

normalIntro.en: See ghost inside the word: aghast means scared as if by a ghost.
normalIntro.cn: 在词里看见 ghost：aghast 就是被吓得见了鬼一般。

normal.en: a + ghast: the ghost has scared your breath away
normal.cn: a+ghast：鬼把你的气都吓没了

normal.en: stand aghast is the anchor collocation
normal.cn: stand aghast 是锚定搭配：惊得呆立

normal.en: aghast at the price, at the news, at the mess
normal.cn: aghast at 常接价格、消息、烂摊子

normal.en: ghost, ghastly, aghast: one frightening family
normal.cn: ghost、ghastly、aghast 同属「惊吓」家族

normal.en: aghast is for the face, agape is for the mouth
normal.cn: aghast 写脸上之惊，agape 写嘴上之张

abstract.en: A face draining white as a door creaks open
abstract.cn: 房门吱呀一响，一张脸瞬间血色尽失

abstract.en: Breath hanging in cold air, stopped mid-cloud
abstract.cn: 呵出的白气凝在半空，呼吸骤停

abstract.en: A juror frozen between verdict slips
abstract.cn: 陪审员捏着两页裁定书，僵在原地

examples.en: The court's verdict left the accused's family aghast.
examples.cn: 法庭判决让被告家人惊骇不已。

examples.en: Neighbours stood aghast as the crane toppled across the street.
examples.cn: 吊车横倒在街对面，邻居们看得目瞪口呆。

examples.en: She was aghast at how quickly the ancient carvings had been defaced.
examples.cn: 古代石刻竟被破坏得如此之快，她深感震惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额·嘎斯特」——见到 ghost（鬼），吓得倒抽一口冷气「嘎」的一声。谐音仅助记，并非词源。

root: 古英语 gāst「灵魂、气息」（一般认为出自印欧词根 *gheys-「激动、惊惧」，与 ghost 同源）派生动词 agasten「吓唬」，其过去分词 agast 经拼写演变定为 aghast；本义「气息被吓跑」，即「惊骇失色」。

sensesIntro.en: One frightened breath serves both the shock of danger and the shock of outrage.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一次被吓住的呼吸，既回应危险，也回应不义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: breath stopped by sudden horror
core.cn: 核心意象：被突如其来的惊骇止住的呼吸

branches.en: terror that freezes the body
branches.cn: 令身体僵住的恐惧

branches.en: breath knocked out by what is seen
branches.cn: 被眼前之事夺走的呼吸

branches.en: horror at a moral wrong
branches.cn: 对不义之事的震惊

branches.en: public dismay at scandal
branches.cn: 对丑闻的公愤

branches.en: words failing the frightened
branches.cn: 吓坏了的人说不出话

intro.en: The word is a fossilized past participle: a- (intensive) plus gast, the root of ghost.
intro.cn: 该词是石化的过去分词：加强前缀 a- 加词根 gast（ghost 的本源）。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestry; Latin expresses horror through its own roots.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语用自有词根表达「惊骇」。

惊骇地（古旧罕用）

definition_zh: 敏捷的；灵活的；（思维）机敏的
definition_en: able to move quickly and easily; able to think quickly and clearly
core_image: 猫穿屋檐：起步、变向、落地一气呵成
scene: 篮球场上，控卫的变向快得让防守者扑空。The agile guard changed direction so fast that his marker fell away.
sceneCN: 这里 agile 是「身手敏捷的」（第 1 个义项：动作迅速灵活）；句意是控卫变向极快，防守者完全扑空。

senses.title: Able to move quickly and easily
senses.definition: physically quick, light, and well-coordinated in movement
senses.definitionCN: 身体动作迅速、轻巧、协调
senses.example: The agile guard changed direction so fast that his marker fell away.
senses.exampleCN: 控卫变向极快，防守者完全扑空。
senses.why: The Latin agere means to drive, to do; what is agile is ready to act at once, body answering without delay.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 agere 意为「驱动、行动」；agile 之「敏」正是随时可动、身体毫不迟疑地响应。

senses.title: Able to think quickly and clearly
senses.definition: mentally quick, able to grasp and shift ideas without effort
senses.definitionCN: 反应快，能毫不费力地理解并转换思路
senses.example: Her agile mind turned the puzzle inside out within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 几分钟内，她就用机敏的头脑把难题翻了个底朝天。
senses.why: A mind that acts the way an agile body does—starting, stopping, turning—is the same quality carried into thought.
senses.whyCN: 头脑像敏捷的身体一样起、停、转向——同一品质移入思维即「机敏」。

senses.title: Adaptable in organization or process
senses.definition: able to change plans quickly in response to new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 能随新情况迅速调整计划与做法
senses.example: Startups survive by staying agile while giants reorganize.
senses.exampleCN: 巨头还在重组，初创公司靠灵活应变活了下来。
senses.why: An institution that moves like an agile body survives change; the bodily image extends to companies and methods.
senses.whyCN: 像敏捷身体一样行动的机构才能应变；身体意象扩展到公司与工作方法。

intro.en: From Latin agilis, from agere (to drive, to do), through French agile into English.
intro.cn: 源自拉丁语 agilis，出于 agere（驱动、行动），经法语 agile 进入英语。

items.en: The root *h2eg- (to drive, to move) underlies agere and its large family.
items.cn: 一般认为词根 *h2eg-（驱动、移动）是 agere 及其庞大家族的远源。

items.en: agere meant to drive, to act; agilis meant easy to move, nimble.
items.cn: 拉丁语 agere 意为「驱动、行动」，agilis 意为「易动的、灵巧的」。

items.en: agile passed through French with the sense of nimble and quick.
items.cn: agile 经法语传入，保留「灵巧、迅捷」之义。

items.en: Borrowed first of bodies, then of minds and wits.
items.cn: 十五世纪借入英语，先指身体，后用于头脑才智。

items.en: The 2001 Agile Manifesto fixed the third sense: adaptive, iterative ways of working.
items.cn: 2001 年《敏捷宣言》确立了第三义：适应性、迭代式的工作方式。

note.en: Agile highlights ease in changing direction; nimble adds lightness, dexterity adds skill of hands.
note.cn: agile 强调变向之自如；nimble 多一层轻巧，dexterity 强调手上的功夫。

scene: 暴雨来临前，那只猫在湿滑的屋脊上快速移动，几乎没有发出声音，几步就跳到了阁楼窗台。Its agility allowed the cat to cross the wet rooftops in seconds.

senses.title: The ability to move quickly and easily
senses.titleCN: 身手的敏捷；动作的灵活
senses.definition: the physical quality of being able to move fast, lightly, and without difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 身体快速、轻巧、毫无滞碍地移动的能力
senses.example: The goalkeeper dived across the goal with surprising agility.
senses.exampleCN: 守门员以惊人的敏捷飞身扑向球门。
senses.why: The image of the cat on the rooftop is pure body skill: light steps, quick turns, no stumbles.
senses.whyCN: 屋脊上猫的画面是纯粹的身体技能：脚步轻、转身快、绝不绊倒，这正是本义的核心。

senses.title: Quickness of mind or adaptation
senses.definition: the ability to think, learn, or change plans quickly and effectively
senses.definitionCN: 快速思考、学习或调整计划并有效应对的能力
senses.example: Her mental agility let her switch between the two arguments without notes.
senses.exampleCN: 她思维敏捷，不看讲稿就能在两个论点之间自如切换。
senses.why: When the body image is lifted to the mind, thinking becomes the thing that jumps and turns without delay.
senses.whyCN: 把身体的画面抬升到头脑，思考就成了那种跳跃、转身毫不迟延的动作，于是长出抽象义项。

senses.title: Flexibility of an organization or system
senses.definition: the quality of a company or system being able to change and respond quickly
senses.definitionCN: 公司或系统能够迅速变化和回应的品质
senses.example: The startup survived the crisis because of its agility.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创公司靠自身的应变灵活度渡过了危机。
senses.why: The same lightness of movement applies to how a whole group shifts direction under pressure.
senses.whyCN: 同样的轻巧移动用在整体上，就是一个团体在压力下迅速转向的方式，义项由此扩展到组织层面。

intro.en: Agility comes from the Latin adjective agilis (movable, nimble), built on agere (to drive, to do), and reached English through French in the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: agility 源自拉丁语形容词 agilis（可动的、灵巧的），建立在动词 agere（驱动、做）之上，十五世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ag- meant to drive or to move something forward.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ag- 意为驱动、推动某物前进。

items.en: Agere meant to drive or to act, and agilis described things that move easily.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、行动，agilis 形容容易移动的事物。

items.en: The word passed into Old French as agilite, keeping the sense of nimbleness.
items.cn: 该词以 agilite 进入古法语，保留灵巧之意。

items.en: English adopted agility in the fifteenth century, first for physical quickness.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收 agility，最初指身体上的敏捷。

items.en: Modern usage extends the word to mental quickness and organizational flexibility.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词扩展到思维敏捷与组织灵活性。

note.en: Agility is often confused with words of similar spelling or related meaning.
note.cn: agility 常与拼写相近或意义相关的词混淆。

definition_zh: 搅动；摇动；使焦虑；煽动；鼓动
definition_en: to shake or stir something, to make someone anxious, or to campaign publicly for a cause
core_image: 用长柄勺不停搅动一锅浓汤，让沉底的东西翻上来
scene: 厨房里，厨师用长柄勺快速搅动锅里的浓汤。She agitated the soup so the cream would not settle at the bottom.
sceneCN: 这里 agitate 是「搅动」（第 1 个义项：反复摇动或搅拌液体与混合物）；句意为她搅动汤，免得奶油沉在锅底。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、长柄勺、灶台。

pos.zh: 动词：搅动；摇动；使焦虑；煽动

derivatives.zh: 由 agitate 加 -ion 构成，义为「搅动；焦虑；鼓动」

senses.title: To stir a liquid
senses.definition: to shake or stir a liquid or mixture so that its parts move and mix
senses.definitionCN: 反复摇动或搅拌液体或混合物，使各部分流动混合
senses.example: She agitated the soup so the cream would not settle.
senses.exampleCN: 她搅动汤，免得奶油沉下去。
senses.why: Latin agitare was the frequentative of agere 'to do, drive', so it meant 'to keep driving something about'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agitare 是 agere「做、驱动」的反复形式，意为「反复把某物来回驱赶」。

senses.title: To make someone anxious
senses.definition: to disturb someone's calm and make them feel nervous or upset
senses.definitionCN: 打破某人的平静，使其感到紧张或烦躁
senses.example: The strange phone calls agitated her all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 那些奇怪的电话让她整晚心神不宁。
senses.why: If liquid can be stirred, so can the mind: the same word describes thoughts kept from settling.
senses.whyCN: 既然液体能被搅动，心也能被搅动：同一个词描述无法平静下来的思绪。

senses.title: To campaign for a cause
senses.definition: to argue publicly and persistently for a political or social change
senses.definitionCN: 公开而持续地为某项政治或社会变革奔走呼吁
senses.example: The group agitated for cleaner water in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团体为山谷里更清洁的水源奔走呼吁。
senses.why: Public opinion is another liquid: the campaigner keeps stirring it until it moves.
senses.whyCN: 舆论也是一种液体：鼓动者不断搅动它，直到它流动起来。

senses.title: To stir up debate
senses.definition: to provoke discussion, unrest, or strong feeling among a group
senses.definitionCN: 在一群人中激起讨论、骚动或强烈情绪
senses.example: The question agitated the whole committee for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题在委员会里激起了数周的争论。
senses.why: A stirred pot does not stay still; a stirred group of people will not either.
senses.whyCN: 被搅动的锅不会静止；被搅动的人群也不会。

senses.title: To shake a container
senses.definition: to shake a vessel or device so that its contents move
senses.definitionCN: 摇动容器或装置，使里面的东西运动
senses.example: Agitate the bottle before pouring the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 倒药之前先摇匀瓶子。
senses.why: This is the physical core at its simplest: a closed vessel is made to move so its contents follow.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的物理核心：让封闭的容器运动起来，里面的东西随之而动。

intro.en: Agitate is the Latin verb 'to keep driving about', a frequentative built on agere.
intro.cn: agitate 是拉丁语「反复驱动」的动词，由 agere 的反复形式构成。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive, or set in motion, the base of act, agent and agenda.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使运动」，是 act、agent、agenda 的词基。

items.en: The frequentative agitare meant to keep driving or shaking something, to set it in repeated motion.
items.cn: 反复动词 agitare 意为「反复驱动或摇动某物」，使其持续运动。

items.en: The participle agitatus described something shaken or kept in motion, and also a troubled mind.
items.cn: 分词 agitatus 描述被摇动、处于运动中的事物，也指不安的心。

items.en: English borrowed the word first for physical stirring and shaking.
items.cn: 英语最初借入这个词，用来指物理上的搅动与摇动。

items.en: By the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries it also meant to stir up feeling or to campaign politically.
items.cn: 到十八、十九世纪，它又指搅动情绪或在政治上进行鼓动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of stirring and campaigning.
note.cn: 形近组收同根词族；近义组收表示搅动与鼓动的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for stirring, nervous unrest, or public campaigning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「搅动；焦躁；鼓动」，兼指物理与情绪、政治三方面。

entries.definition: A device that stirs, or a person who campaigns for change.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「搅拌器；鼓动者」，既指搅动的装置，也指推动变革的人。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning nervous, upset, or physically shaken.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「焦虑不安的；被摇动的」。

entries.definition: To move a spoon or other object around in a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「搅拌」，指用勺等物在液体中转动。

entries.definition: To interrupt someone's peace or make them worried.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打扰；使不安」，指打断平静或让人担忧。

entries.definition: To take part in organized activity aimed at a political or social goal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「开展运动；奔走」，指为政治或社会目标组织活动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to a stirring spoon, a restless mind and a speaker working up a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与搅拌的勺子、不安的心以及煽动人群的演讲者联系起来。

normal.en: AGITATE contains ag- 'do' and -itate, a suffix of repeated action: to keep doing something to a liquid.
normal.cn: agitate 含 ag-「做」与表示反复动作的 -itate：对液体反复做某个动作。

normal.en: Picture a spoon going round and round in a pot of soup.
normal.cn: 想象一把勺子在汤锅里一圈圈地转。

normal.en: A shaken bottle of medicine must be agitated before use.
normal.cn: 药瓶用前要摇匀，这个动作就是 agitate。

normal.en: When worry stirs your thoughts, you feel agitated.
normal.cn: 当忧虑搅动思绪时，你就感到心神不宁。

normal.en: A campaigner agitates public opinion the way a spoon agitates soup.
normal.cn: 鼓动者搅动舆论，就像勺子搅动汤。

abstract.en: To agitate is to refuse to let something settle.
abstract.cn: 搅动，就是不让某样东西沉淀下来。

abstract.en: The same motion calms soup and unsettles people.
abstract.cn: 同一种运动，能让汤均匀，也能让人心不安。

abstract.en: Political agitation is a mind kept deliberately in motion.
abstract.cn: 政治鼓动，就是一颗被有意搅动的心。

examples.en: Agitate the paint before you open the can.
examples.cn: 打开漆罐之前先把它摇匀。

examples.en: The waiting crowd grew agitated as the hours passed.
examples.cn: 随着时间一小时小时过去，等候的人群越来越焦躁。

examples.en: For years the villagers agitated for a new road.
examples.cn: 多年来村民们一直为新修一条路而奔走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿吉，忒特」：阿吉忒特别，总爱搅动锅里的汤，也搅动大家的情绪。

root: 拉丁语 agere（做、驱动）的反复形式 agitare（反复驱动、摇动），过去分词 agitatus 进入英语，核心意象是「反复搅动」，由物及心，再到政治鼓动。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with physical stirring, extends to a disturbed mind, and ends with public campaigning and debate.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从物理搅动开始，延伸到被搅乱的心，最后落在公开鼓动与争论上。

core.en: KEEP SOMETHING IN MOTION
core.cn: 让某物持续运动

branches.en: a liquid stirred in a pot
branches.cn: 锅里被搅动的液体

branches.en: a closed vessel shaken
branches.cn: 被摇动的封闭容器

branches.en: a mind kept from settling
branches.cn: 无法平静的心

branches.en: opinion stirred for a cause
branches.cn: 为某项事业被搅动的舆论

branches.en: a group stirred into debate
branches.cn: 被搅起争论的一群人

intro.en: Agitate is the frequentative member of the ag- family, marking repeated or vigorous action.
intro.cn: agitate 是 ag- 词族中的反复成员，标记反复或剧烈的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere 'do' plus the frequentative suffix -itare produced agitare, the source of the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere「做」加上反复后缀 -itare 造出 agitare，成为这一组的源头。

items.example: His agitation showed in his shaking hands.
items.exampleCN: 他双手发抖，显出内心的焦躁。

items.meaning: a device or person that stirs
items.example: The washing machine has a central agitator.
items.exampleCN: 这台洗衣机中央有一个搅拌器。

items.example: The agitated patient could not sit still.
It was an agitating piece of news.
items.exampleCN: 那是一条令人不安的消息。
这份传单纯粹是鼓动性的。

items.meaning: political art or writing meant to stir support
items.meaningCN: 鼓动宣传；政治宣传作品
items.example: The play was dismissed as agitprop.
items.exampleCN: 这部剧被讥为政治宣传。

items.meaning: in a nervous or shaken manner
items.example: She paced agitatedly by the door.
items.exampleCN: 她在门口焦躁地来回踱步。

items.example: He remained unagitated during the storm.

latinEntries.meaning: to do, drive, set in motion

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被摇动的；被搅动的；不安的
